children.title: Bregman Three-Point Principle
children.top_down_role: The central comparison family underlying mirror potential analysis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite convex variant of the proximal comparison principle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[x_+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{\eta\langle g,x\rangle+\eta\psi(x)+D_h(x,x_0)\}.\] Suppose proximal optimality admits \(s_+\in\partial\psi(x_+)\) and \(n_+\in N_C(x_+)\) satisfying \(0=\eta(g+s_+)+\nabla h(x_+)-\nabla h(x_0)+n_+\). Then every \(u\in C\) satisfies \[\eta\bigl(\langle g,x_+-u\rangle+\psi(x_+)-\psi(u)\bigr)\le D_h(u,x_0)-D_h(u,x_+)-D_h(x_+,x_0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal three-point comparison extends to a convex term retained exactly in the subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and the displayed minimum is attained.
\(h\) is convex and differentiable wherever the divergences are evaluated.
\(\psi\) is proper and convex, \(\eta>0\), and the displayed decomposed optimality condition holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Bregman Three-Point Inequality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic identity underlying proximal three-point inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For all admissible \(a,b,c\), \[\langle\nabla h(b)-\nabla h(c),a-b\rangle=D_h(a,c)-D_h(a,b)-D_h(b,c).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mirror-gradient displacement paired with a comparison direction equals a telescoping difference of three divergences.
assumptions_latex: All displayed function values and divergences are finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Three-Point Identity
Bregman Three-Point Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational inequality for one Bregman proximal step on a convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be convex, let \(h\) be convex and differentiable on a set containing \(C\), and define \(D_h(x,y)=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle\). For \(x_0\in C\), \(g\) in the dual space, and \(\eta>0\), suppose \(x_+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_0)\}\). Then every \(u\in C\) satisfies
\[
\eta\langle g,x_+-u\rangle\le D_h(u,x_0)-D_h(u,x_+)-D_h(x_+,x_0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bregman proximal step compares to every feasible point through a telescoping difference of three divergences.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and the displayed minimizer exists.
\(h\) is convex and differentiable wherever the divergences are evaluated.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle, hypotheses, and content kind are mathematically appropriate, but no citation or inspectable locator supports the proximal three-point inequality.

children.title: Bregman Diameter Bound
children.top_down_role: The geometry-size organizer for uniform and localized mirror complexity.

children.title: Uniform Bregman-Diameter Regime
children.top_down_role: Uniform divergence control over the comparison domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient condition for finite uniform Bregman diameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty compact subset of \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), and suppose \(h\) is continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(C\). Then \(D_h\) is continuous on \(C\times C\), so \[\Omega_C:=\max_{x,y\in C}D_h(x,y)<\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact comparison set strictly inside the continuously differentiable region of the generator has finite uniform Bregman diameter.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.title: Compact Interior Sufficient Condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Domain Does Not Ensure Uniform Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary singularities can make the divergence diameter infinite even on a compact domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\Delta_n\), \(n\ge2\), let \(h(x)=\sum_i x_i\log x_i\), so \(D_h(x,y)=\sum_i x_i\log(x_i/y_i)\) on its effective domain. For \(k\ge2\), set \(y^{(k)}=(1/k,1-1/k,0,\ldots,0)\). Then \[D_h(e_1,y^{(k)})=\log k\to\infty,\] although \(\Delta_n\) is compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entropy divergence has infinite pairwise diameter on the compact simplex because its reference point may approach a zero coordinate.
assumptions_latex: Relative entropy uses the standard extended-value conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Domain Does Not Ensure Uniform Divergence
Uniform Bregman-Diameter Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global divergence bound over all admissible ordered pairs in the comparison domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty convex comparison domain \(C\) and a Bregman divergence \(D_h\), the uniform Bregman-diameter regime holds with a constant \(\Omega<\infty\) when
\[
\sup_{(x,y)\in (C\times C)\cap\operatorname{dom}D_h}D_h(x,y)\le \Omega.
\]
Consequently, every admissible initialization-comparator pair \((u,x_0)\in(C\times C)\cap\operatorname{dom}D_h\) satisfies \(D_h(u,x_0)\le\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One finite constant bounds the Bregman divergence over every admissible ordered pair in the comparison domain.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty convex comparison domain.
\(D_h\) is a Bregman divergence with domain \(\operatorname{dom}D_h\subseteq C\times C\) for the pairs under consideration.

children.title: Localized Bregman-Radius Regime
children.top_down_role: Reference-point or solution-relative divergence control.

knowledge_statements.title: Localized Bregman-Radius Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Divergence bound relative to one comparator or a designated solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an initialization \(x_0\in C\) and a nonempty comparator set \(U\subseteq C\). The localized Bregman-radius regime holds with radius \(R_h<\infty\) when
\[
\sup_{u\in U}D_h(u,x_0)\le R_h^2.
\]
For solution-relative analysis one may take \(U=X^*\), the set of minimizers, or require only one \(x^*\in X^*\) satisfying \(D_h(x^*,x_0)\le R_h^2\). No bound on \(D_h(x,y)\) for arbitrary \(x,y\in C\) is implied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only divergence from the chosen initialization to relevant comparators or solutions is bounded; the whole domain may have infinite diameter.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The localized condition is precise and appropriately distinguishes comparator-relative control from uniform diameter control, but it has no supporting citation or locator.

children.title: Unbounded Bregman Geometry
children.top_down_role: Mirror setups without a useful uniform diameter certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Convexity Forces Infinite Bregman Diameter on Unbounded Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General sufficient condition for failure of uniform Bregman-diameter control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be an unbounded convex subset of a finite-dimensional normed space, and let \(h\) be differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a convex neighborhood of \(C\), where \(\mu>0\). Then \(D_h(x,y)\ge(\mu/2)\lVert x-y\rVert^2\) for all \(x,y\in C\), and therefore \(\sup_{x,y\in C}D_h(x,y)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every strongly convex mirror map has infinite global Bregman diameter on an unbounded comparison set.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and unbounded in finite dimensions.
\(h\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a convex neighborhood of \(C\), with \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convexity Forces Infinite Bregman Diameter on Unbounded Sets
Unbounded Bregman Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform diameter without failure of comparator-relative analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(h(x)=\tfrac12\lVert x\rVert_2^2\). Then \(D_h(x,y)=\tfrac12\lVert x-y\rVert_2^2\), so
\[
\sup_{x,y\in C}D_h(x,y)=+\infty.
\]
Thus no finite uniform Bregman-diameter certificate exists. Nevertheless, for every fixed initialization \(x_0\in C\) and finite comparator \(u\in C\), the localized potential \(D_h(u,x_0)\) is finite. Bounds based on this potential remain meaningful when a suitable comparator is known.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Euclidean geometry on an unbounded domain has infinite global Bregman diameter, although every fixed comparator has finite divergence from the initialization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Euclidean example correctly exhibits the stated failure boundary, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Canonical Mirror Setups
children.top_down_role: Standard pairings of domains, norms, and distance-generating functions.

children.title: Simplex–Entropy Setup
children.top_down_role: Entropic geometry for probability-simplex domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form entropy mirror update on the probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\in\operatorname{ri}\Delta_n\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\eta>0\). The unique minimizer of \[\min_{x\in\Delta_n}\{\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_h(x,y)\}\] is \[x_i^+=\frac{y_i e^{-\eta g_i}}{\sum_{j=1}^n y_j e^{-\eta g_j}},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entropy-prox minimization produces the multiplicative-weights or exponentiated-gradient update.
knowledge_statements.title: Exponentiated-Gradient Simplex Prox Step

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp prox-radius bound from the uniform distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(u=(1/n,\ldots,1/n)\) and every \(x\in\Delta_n\), \[D_h(x,u)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\log(nx_i)=\log n-H(x)\le\log n,\] where \(H(x)=-\sum_i x_i\log x_i\). Equality holds exactly at the vertices of \(\Delta_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entropy divergence from the uniform distribution is at most log n, sharply at simplex vertices.
knowledge_statements.title: Logarithmic Entropy Radius
Simplex–Entropy Setup
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-entropy mirror geometry on the probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On the simplex \(\Delta_n=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=1\}\), choose the negative entropy \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\log x_i\), with \(0\log0=0\). For \(y\) in the relative interior,
\[
D_h(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\log\frac{x_i}{y_i}.
\]
Moreover, \(D_h(x,y)\ge\tfrac12\lVert x-y\rVert_1^2\). Hence \(h\) is one-strongly convex relative to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_1\), whose dual norm is \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative entropy equips the probability simplex with relative entropy divergence and strong convexity in the ℓ1 norm.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entropy representation and Pinsker constant are standard and match the simplex setup, but the nontrivial strong-convexity claim requires an authoritative citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Box-p-Norm Geometry Family
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise and norm-adapted geometries for product domains.

children.title: Box-Domain Setups
children.top_down_role: Mirror setups specialized to bounded Cartesian-product domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit update for the weighted quadratic box setup without an additional composite term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\prod_i[\ell_i,u_i]\), \(h(x)=\tfrac12\sum_i a_i x_i^2\), and \(\psi=0\), the unique Bregman proximal point satisfies \[(x_+)_i=\Pi_{[\ell_i,u_i]}\!\left(y_i-\frac{\eta g_i}{a_i}\right)=\min\{u_i,\max\{\ell_i,y_i-\eta g_i/a_i\}\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted quadratic mirror step on a box is a diagonally scaled step followed by independent coordinate clipping.
assumptions_latex: There is no additional composite term.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the ith interval

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Clipping Box Prox Step

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic cost of evaluating the explicit clipping update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given dense vectors \(y,g,a,\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\), the coordinate-clipping formula evaluates the weighted quadratic box proximal point using \(O(n)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(n)\) output storage; no coupled optimization subproblem is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The explicit box proximal update is evaluated in one pass over the coordinates.
assumptions_latex: All coordinate data are available explicitly.
Scalar arithmetic and comparisons have unit cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Time Box Prox Evaluation
Box-Domain Setups
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted quadratic mirror geometry for axis-aligned boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) with widths \(w_i=u_i-\ell_i>0\), and choose weights \(a_i>0\). The separable generator
\[
h(x)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i^2
\]
has divergence \(D_h(x,y)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^n a_i(x_i-y_i)^2\). It is one-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert z\rVert_a=(\sum_i a_i z_i^2)^{1/2}\), and every \(x,y\in C\) satisfy \(D_h(x,y)\le\tfrac12\sum_i a_iw_i^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagonal quadratic generator yields separable weighted Euclidean geometry and an explicit diameter bound on any axis-aligned box.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted quadratic representation, strong convexity, and box diameter bound are consistent, but no supporting source is cited.

children.title: p-Norm Setups
children.top_down_role: Mirror setups adapted to p-norm domain geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-dual representation of the scaled squared p-norm generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q=p/(p-1)\), the Fenchel conjugate of \(h_p(x)=\|x\|_p^2/(2(p-1))\) is \[h_p^*(s)=\frac{p-1}{2}\|s\|_q^2.\] Consequently, whenever the unconstrained mirror step is admissible, \[x_+=\nabla h_p^*(\nabla h_p(y)-\eta g).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate generator is a reciprocally scaled squared q-norm, yielding the unconstrained update in dual coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The displayed conjugate-gradient evaluation lies in its differentiability domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate p–q Mirror Geometry

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp endpoint boundary of the scaled squared p-norm mirror family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge2\), the function \(x\mapsto\tfrac12\|x\|_1^2\) is not strictly convex. Indeed, for \(x=e_1\), \(y=e_2\), and \(0<t<1\), \[\|tx+(1-t)y\|_1^2=1=t\|x\|_1^2+(1-t)\|y\|_1^2.\] Therefore the squared-norm construction cannot be extended to \(p=1\) with a positive strong-convexity modulus relative to \(\|\cdot\|_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared one-norm is flat along simplex segments, so the strongly convex squared p-norm construction requires p strictly above one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tfrac12\|\cdot\|_1^2\) is not strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|_1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Failure at the One-Norm Endpoint

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient and Divergence of the Squared p-Norm Generator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit differential representation of the canonical p-norm generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(1<p\le2\) and \(x
e0\), \[ igl(
abla h_p(x) igr)_i= rac{\|x\|_p^{2-p}}{p-1}|x_i|^{p-2}x_i,\qquad h_p(x)= rac{\|x\|_p^2}{2(p-1)},\] with \(
abla h_p(0)=0\). Hence \[D_{h_p}(x,y)= rac{\|x\|_p^2-\|y\|_p^2}{2(p-1)}-\langle
abla h_p(y),x-yangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared p-norm generator has an explicit duality-map gradient and Bregman divergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Gradient and Divergence of the Squared p-Norm Generator
p-Norm Setups
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-type mirror geometry for spaces with exponent between one and two.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1<p\le2\) and let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex. The generator
\[
h_p(x)=\frac{1}{2(p-1)}\lVert x\rVert_p^2
\]
is one-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_p\). Thus its Bregman divergence satisfies \(D_{h_p}(x,y)\ge\tfrac12\lVert x-y\rVert_p^2\) wherever \(h_p\) is differentiable. Linear terms are measured in the dual norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_q\), where \(q=p/(p-1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled squared ℓp norm supplies strong convexity in ℓp geometry for exponents between one and two.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled squared \(p\)-norm representation is appropriate for \(1<p\le2\), but its strong-convexity modulus needs a cited authoritative source and locator.

children.title: Coordinatewise Product Geometry
children.top_down_role: Separable geometric structure underlying coordinate-scaled prox mappings.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product Strong Convexity and Diameter Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of blockwise curvature and divergence-size certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each \(h_i\) is \(\mu_i\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|_i\), define \(\|x\|_\mu^2=\sum_i\mu_i\|x_i\|_i^2\). Then \[D_h(x,y)\ge\tfrac12\|x-y\|_\mu^2.\] If also \(D_{h_i}(x_i,y_i)\le\Omega_i\) on \(C_i\times C_i\), then \[D_h(x,y)\le\sum_i\Omega_i\quad(x,y\in C).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blockwise curvature forms a weighted product norm, while blockwise divergence diameters add.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tfrac12\|x-y\|_\mu^2\le D_h(x,y)\le\sum_i\Omega_i\) whenever the block diameter assumptions hold.

notation.meaning: uniform divergence bound for block i

knowledge_statements.title: Product Strong Convexity and Diameter Aggregation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of blockwise proximal decomposition to an additive convex composite term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\prod_i C_i\), \(h(x)=\sum_i h_i(x_i)\), and \(\psi(x)=\sum_i\psi_i(x_i)\). If every block minimizer set \[M_i=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z_i\in C_i}\{\eta\langle g_i,z_i\rangle+\eta\psi_i(z_i)+D_{h_i}(z_i,y_i)\}\] is nonempty, then \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in C}\{\eta\langle g,z\rangle+\eta\psi(z)+D_h(z,y)\}=\prod_i M_i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Product constraints, a separable generator, and a separable composite term reduce the proximal problem exactly to independent block problems.
assumptions_latex: Every displayed block minimizer set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Product Proximal Separability
Coordinatewise Product Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable generators decompose divergence and Bregman proximal minimization across coordinate blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\prod_{i=1}^m C_i\) and \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m h_i(x_i)\), where every \(C_i\) is convex and every \(h_i\) is convex and differentiable wherever the relevant divergences are evaluated. Then, for every admissible \(x,y\in C\),
\[
D_h(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^m D_{h_i}(x_i,y_i).
\]
Given \(\eta>0\), \(y=(y_i)_{i=1}^m\in C\), and \(g=(g_i)_{i=1}^m\) in the product dual space, suppose each block minimizer set
\[
M_i=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z_i\in C_i}\{\eta\langle g_i,z_i\rangle+D_{h_i}(z_i,y_i)\}
\]
is nonempty. Then
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in C}\{\eta\langle g,z\rangle+D_h(z,y)\}=\prod_{i=1}^m M_i.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a product domain and separable mirror generator, the divergence is the sum of the block divergences, and the proximal minimizer set is the Cartesian product of the block minimizer sets.
assumptions_latex: \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m h_i(x_i)\), with each \(h_i\) convex and differentiable wherever its divergence is evaluated.
\(\eta>0\), \(y\in C\), and every block minimizer set \(M_i\) is nonempty.

children.title: Norm-Adaptation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Choice of p-norm geometry according to domain shape or oracle scale.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized criterion for comparing admissible mirror geometries in the standard bounded-oracle analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each candidate setup \(r\), suppose \(h_r\) is normalized to be one-strongly convex in \(\|\cdot\|_{(r)}\), \(D_{h_r}(u,x_0)\le\Omega_r\), and \(\|g_t\|_{(r),*}\le G_r\). With the same horizon and standard mirror analysis, optimizing the stepsize orders the geometry-dependent leading factor by \(G_r\sqrt{\Omega_r}\), equivalently by \(\Omega_rG_r^2\). Thus a bound-adapted choice is \[r\in\operatorname*{argmin}_s\Omega_sG_s^2.\] Comparisons require a common strong-convexity normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among valid normalized mirror setups, select a geometry by minimizing its divergence scale times its squared dual-oracle scale.
assumptions_latex: Every candidate generator is normalized to be one-strongly convex in its associated norm.
The candidate setups are compared within the same standard mirror bound and horizon.

notation.meaning: oracle bound in the dual of candidate norm r
divergence-radius bound for candidate geometry r

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry Selection by Diameter–Dual-Norm Product
Norm-Adaptation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Choosing mirror exponent to approximate ℓ1 geometry with logarithmic dimension cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\ge3\), set \(p=1+1/\log n\) and use \(h_p(x)=\lVert x\rVert_p^2/(2(p-1))\). Since
\[
\lVert x\rVert_p\le\lVert x\rVert_1\le n^{1-1/p}\lVert x\rVert_p
\]
and \(n^{1-1/p}\le e\), the chosen norm is within a universal factor of \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_1\). Meanwhile, the generator scaling satisfies \(1/(p-1)=\log n\). Thus adapting \(p\) near one trades a logarithmic prox scale for dimension-independent norm equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking p just above one approximates ℓ1 geometry within a constant factor while introducing only a logarithmic generator scale.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dimension-adapted exponent and norm-equivalence calculation are correct and the principle fits the leaf, but no source supports the adaptation claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Endpoint Failure of the Squared One-Norm Generator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder-proposed claim belongs primarily to the p-norm setup sibling, not to norm selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared one-norm is flat on simplex segments and is not strongly convex in the one-norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tfrac12\|\cdot\|_1^2\) has no positive strong-convexity modulus with respect to \(\|\cdot\|_1\).
review_flags: misplaced_claim: canonical home is p-Norm Setups because this is the endpoint boundary of that generator family
knowledge_statements.title: Endpoint Failure of the Squared One-Norm Generator

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is the seed logarithmic-dimension exponent choice and the normalized diameter–dual-norm selection criterion. The builder's p=1 generator counterexample was deferred as canonically owned by p-Norm Setups. Concrete box generators and product decomposition were also excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Matrix-Spectral Geometry Family
children.top_down_role: Mirror geometries for positive-semidefinite and spectral domains.

children.title: Positive-Semidefinite Matrix Setups
children.top_down_role: Mirror geometry for positive-semidefinite feasible domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form entropy-prox update on trace-one positive-definite matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\in\mathbb S_{++}^d\) satisfy \(\operatorname{Tr}Y=1\), let \(G\in\mathbb S^d\), and let \(\eta>0\). The unique solution of \[\min_{X\succeq0,\,\operatorname{Tr}X=1}\{\eta\langle G,X\rangle+D_h(X,Y)\}\] is \[X^+=\frac{\exp(\log Y-\eta G)}{\operatorname{Tr}\exp(\log Y-\eta G)}.\] No commutativity assumption on \(G\) and \(Y\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The matrix-entropy prox map is the normalized matrix exponential of the previous log-density minus the loss matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Exponentiated-Gradient Mirror Step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Entropy Radius from the Maximally Mixed Center
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp dimension-dependent prox radius on the density-matrix spectrahedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(U=I/d\) and every \(X\succeq0\) with \(\operatorname{Tr}X=1\), \[D_h(X,U)=\operatorname{Tr}(X\log X)+\log d=\log d-S(X)\le\log d,\] where \(S(X)=-\operatorname{Tr}(X\log X)\). Equality holds exactly for rank-one density matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximally mixed matrix has entropy-prox radius log d, attained by pure states.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropy Radius from the Maximally Mixed Center
Positive-Semidefinite Matrix Setups
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-entropy geometry on the trace-one positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On the spectrahedron \(\mathcal{S}_d=\{X\in\mathbb{S}_+^d:\operatorname{Tr}X=1\}\), choose \(h(X)=\operatorname{Tr}(X\log X)\), with the scalar convention \(0\log0=0\). For positive-definite \(Y\in\mathcal{S}_d\),
\[
D_h(X,Y)=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(X(\log X-\log Y)\bigr).
\]
Quantum Pinsker inequality gives \(D_h(X,Y)\ge\tfrac12\lVert X-Y\rVert_*^2\). Hence matrix entropy is one-strongly convex relative to the trace norm, whose dual is the spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix entropy equips trace-one positive-semidefinite matrices with quantum relative entropy and trace-norm strong convexity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The matrix-entropy representation and quantum Pinsker conclusion match the PSD setup, but these nontrivial claims require an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Spectral-Norm Setups
children.top_down_role: Setups adapted to operator-norm or eigenvalue-based scale.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank-Dependent Distortion of the Quadratic Setup
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp comparison between Frobenius and spectral norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(H\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), with \(r=\min\{m,n\}\), \[\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|H\|_F\le\sqrt r\,\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}.\] Both constants are sharp: rank-one matrices attain the first equality, while matrices with \(r\) equal nonzero singular values attain the second. Thus spectral-norm curvature of the quadratic generator is dimension-free, but Frobenius diameter estimates on spectral-norm balls can lose a factor \(r\) after squaring.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sharp Frobenius/spectral norm comparison identifies the rank-dimensional diameter loss of the quadratic setup.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Dependent Distortion of the Quadratic Setup
Spectral-Norm Setups
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic mirror geometry measured against the matrix spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a convex subset of \(\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), equipped with the spectral norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\), and choose \(h(X)=\tfrac12\lVert X\rVert_F^2\). Then
\[
D_h(X,Y)=\frac12\lVert X-Y\rVert_F^2\ge\frac12\lVert X-Y\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2.
\]
Thus \(h\) is one-strongly convex relative to the spectral norm. The corresponding dual norm for subgradients and linear losses is the trace norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared Frobenius norm is strongly convex relative to spectral norm, while trace norm measures the associated dual linear terms.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Frobenius generator gives the stated spectral-norm strong convexity and the dual-norm identification is appropriate, but neither claim is cited.

children.title: Trace-Norm Setups
children.top_down_role: Setups adapted to low-rank-sensitive trace-norm geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Scaling of Quadratic Trace-Norm Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient scaling for scalar quadratic generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_c(X)=\tfrac c2\|X\|_F^2\) on \(\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and let \(r=\min\{m,n\}\). Then \(h_c\) is one-strongly convex relative to \(\|\cdot\|_*\) if and only if \(c\ge r\). Equivalently, \[c\|H\|_F^2\ge\|H\|_*^2\quad\text{for every }H\] holds exactly when \(c\ge r\). Matrices having \(r\) equal nonzero singular values attain the threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among scalar multiples of squared Frobenius norm, the factor r is necessary and sufficient for unit trace-norm strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_c\text{ is one-strongly convex in }\|\cdot\|_*\iff c\ge r\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Scaling of Quadratic Trace-Norm Geometry
Trace-Norm Setups
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-scaled quadratic geometry for rectangular trace-norm domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r=\min\{m,n\}\), equip \(\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) with the trace norm, and choose
\[
h(X)=\frac r2\lVert X\rVert_F^2.
\]
Because \(\lVert H\rVert_*\le\sqrt r\lVert H\rVert_F\), its divergence satisfies \(D_h(X,Y)=\tfrac r2\lVert X-Y\rVert_F^2\ge\tfrac12\lVert X-Y\rVert_*^2\). Hence \(h\) is one-strongly convex relative to the trace norm. On \(C=\{X:\lVert X\rVert_*\le R\}\), one also has \(D_h(X,Y)\le2rR^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling squared Frobenius norm by matrix rank dimension produces trace-norm strong convexity and a finite bound on trace-norm balls.
assumptions_latex: For the diameter bound, \(\lVert X\rVert_*,\lVert Y\rVert_*\le R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dimension-scaled quadratic representation, trace-norm strong convexity, and stated ball bound are consistent, but an authoritative citation and locator are absent.

children.title: Eigenvalue Geometry Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship between matrix-domain structure and induced spectral geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eigenvalue Reduction of Spectral Proximal Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of a Frobenius proximal problem to eigenvalue coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(X)=\phi(\lambda(X))\), where \(\phi\) is proper, closed, convex, and permutation invariant. If \(Y=U\operatorname{Diag}(y)U^*\) is Hermitian and \(\tau>0\), then \[\operatorname{prox}_{\tau F}(Y)=U\operatorname{Diag}(z)U^*,\qquad z=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau\phi}(y).\] The matrix proximal point is unique, although the displayed eigenbasis need not be unique within repeated-eigenvalue blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex spectral Frobenius proximal problem preserves the center's eigenspaces and applies the scalar proximal map to its eigenvalues.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, closed, convex, and permutation invariant.
knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue Reduction of Spectral Proximal Problems

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel conjugacy transferred from symmetric eigenvalue functions to Hermitian matrix space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, convex, and permutation invariant, and set \(F(X)=\phi(\lambda(X))\) on Hermitian matrices with the trace inner product. Then \[F^*(Y)=\phi^*(\lambda(Y)).\] Fenchel–Young equality holds precisely when compatible scalar subgradients can be lifted in a common ordered eigenbasis, with the usual freedom inside repeated-eigenvalue blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel conjugacy of a symmetric convex eigenvalue function lifts exactly to Hermitian matrix space, with equality governed by aligned scalar subgradients.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, closed, convex, and permutation invariant.
Hermitian matrix space uses the trace inner product.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate on Hermitian matrix space

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugacy of Convex Spectral Functions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm correspondence for Hermitian matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every Hermitian \(X\) and \(1\le p\le\infty\), \[\|X\|_{S_p}=\||\lambda(X)|\|_p=\|\lambda(X)\|_p.\] If \(1/p+1/q=1\), the dual of \(\|\cdot\|_{S_p}\) under the trace pairing is \(\|\cdot\|_{S_q}\); in particular, the trace and operator norms are dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hermitian matrix's Schatten norm is the p-norm of its eigenvalues, and conjugate Schatten norms are dual under the trace pairing.
knowledge_statements.title: Schatten–Eigenvalue Norm Correspondence
Eigenvalue Geometry Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient correspondence between symmetric eigenvalue functions and unitarily invariant convex matrix functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, convex, and invariant under coordinate permutations, and define \(F(X)=\phi(\lambda(X))\) on the Hermitian matrices. Then \(F\) is convex and unitarily invariant. If \(X=U\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda(X))U^*\), then \(y\in\partial\phi(\lambda(X))\) implies \(U\operatorname{Diag}(y)U^*\in\partial F(X)\). Conversely, every \(G\in\partial F(X)\) admits a simultaneous eigenbasis with \(X\), ordered consistently within repeated-eigenvalue blocks, such that its eigenvalue vector belongs to \(\partial\phi(\lambda(X))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric convex geometry on eigenvalues lifts to unitarily invariant matrix geometry, with aligned scalar and matrix subgradients.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is Hermitian and \(\lambda(X)\) is ordered consistently.
\(\phi\) is proper, closed, convex, and permutation invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial F(X)\) is obtained by lifting aligned elements of \(\partial\phi(\lambda(X))\) through eigenvectors of \(X\).

notation.meaning: ordered eigenvalue vector of the Hermitian matrix X

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the eigenvalue-geometry leaf and is mathematically plausible, but the nontrivial spectral subdifferential correspondence has no inspectable citation. The plain statement also omits the converse characterization and repeated-eigenvalue alignment qualification.

children.title: Prox-Setup Quality
children.top_down_role: Joint organization of geometric efficiency and prox-subproblem tractability.

children.title: Geometry-Adapted Domain Size
children.top_down_role: Selection of geometry to control effective domain size.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting a small prox radius as a superior setup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A smaller normalized Bregman radius alone does not establish a better prox setup: the associated dual oracle bound may increase, and \(\sup_{x\in Q}D_h(x,x_1)\) may be infinite on an unbounded or boundary-singular domain. A finite joint geometry factor requires both \(M_*<\infty\) and \(\sup_{x\in Q}D_h(x,x_1)/\sigma<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite or small domain radius is useful only jointly with a finite dual oracle scale.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is strongly convex relative to the selected primal norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite joint geometry factor requires \(M_*<\infty\) and \(\sup_{x\in Q}D_h(x,x_1)/\sigma<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Size-Only Comparison Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint domain-and-oracle scale for comparing equivalent norm normalizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_*\) bound oracle outputs in the dual norm, let \(h\) be \(\sigma\)-strongly convex in the primal norm, and set \(\Omega_h=\sup_{x\in Q}D_h(x,x_1)\). Then \[\Gamma=M_*\sqrt{\frac{2\Omega_h}{\sigma}}\] is invariant under \(\|x\|'=c\|x\|\): \(M_*'=M_*/c\), \(\sigma'=\sigma/c^2\), and \(\Gamma'=\Gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The product of dual oracle magnitude and normalized Bregman radius is invariant under mere norm rescaling.

notation.meaning: Maximum Bregman divergence from the prox center.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Invariant Geometry Quality Product
Geometry-Adapted Domain Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized Bregman radius used to compare mirror geometries on a fixed feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be convex and let \(h:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to a norm \(\|\cdot\|\). For a prox center \(x_1\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}h(x)\), define \(R_h^2(Q;x_1)=2\sup_{x\in Q}D_h(x,x_1)/\sigma\). Then \(\|x-x_1\|^2\le R_h^2(Q;x_1)\) for every \(x\in Q\). Selecting a geometry with smaller finite \(R_h(Q;x_1)\), while retaining manageable dual subgradient norms, reduces the domain-size factor in mirror-method bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mirror geometry is domain-adapted when its normalized Bregman radius is small relative to the associated dual subgradient scale.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex on \(Q\), with \(\sigma>0\).

notation.meaning: normalized Bregman radius of Q about the prox center

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard normalized prox-diameter criterion in mirror-method analysis
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the domain-size leaf, and the radius inequality follows under the stated strong-convexity convention. An authoritative locator is required because the factor-of-two normalization and its role in mirror-method bounds are convention-dependent.

children.title: Prox-Mapping Tractability
children.top_down_role: Computational accessibility of the geometry-dependent prox operation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Convexity Does Not Imply Computational Tractability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes well-posedness from computational accessibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\), the prox mapping over a nonempty closed convex set \(Q\) is \(\Pi_Q(z-\eta g)\). Thus strong convexity may ensure a unique prox point, but it supplies no procedure or complexity bound for computing that point over an arbitrary represented set \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unique prox point need not be computationally accessible; quadratic prox inherits the difficulty of projection onto the set.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convexity Does Not Imply Computational Tractability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural reduction of a product prox problem to component prox problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\prod_{j=1}^mQ_j\), \(h(x)=\sum_{j=1}^m h_j(x_j)\), \(z=(z_j)_j\), and \(g=(g_j)_j\). Then \[\operatorname{Prox}^{h}_{z}(\eta g)=\prod_{j=1}^m\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in Q_j}\{\eta\langle g_j,u\rangle+D_{h_j}(u,z_j)\}.\] Consequently, the product prox reduces to independent component calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product-domain prox with separable geometry decomposes into independent component prox problems.
assumptions_latex: Each \(Q_j\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Separable Prox Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical realization of the constrained prox mapping in Euclidean geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(h(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\), then \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\{\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_h(x,z)\}=\Pi_Q(z-\eta g).\] Hence Euclidean prox accessibility is equivalent to accessibility of projection onto the represented set \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With quadratic geometry, a prox call is a Euclidean projection of the displaced center.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Prox as Projection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Operational Prox-Tractability in a Computation Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation- and accuracy-aware definition of computational accessibility for a Bregman prox call.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a computation model \mathcal M and an encoding I=(Q,h,z,g,\eta). Let \Phi_I(x)=\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_h(x,z)+\iota_Q(x). The prox family is \mathcal M-tractable to objective accuracy \delta>0 if an algorithm returns x_\delta\in Q satisfying \Phi_I(x_\delta)-\inf_x\Phi_I(x)\le\delta using at most C_{\mathrm{prox}}^{\mathcal M}(|I|,\delta) operations, where the encoding, permitted primitives, and finite cost function are specified. Exact tractability is the analogous requirement for an exact minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prox tractability is defined relative to an input representation, accuracy criterion, computation model, and finite cost bound.
assumptions_latex: The encoded prox problem has a finite attained minimum.
The computation model and permitted primitives are fixed.

notation.meaning: prox-call cost in computation model \mathcal M

knowledge_statements.title: Operational Prox-Tractability in a Computation Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion from prox-subproblem objective accuracy to distance accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If h is \sigma-strongly convex on Q with respect to \|\cdot\|, then \Phi_I(x)=\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_h(x,z)+\iota_Q(x) is \sigma-strongly convex on Q. For its unique minimizer x^+, every feasible x_\delta satisfying \Phi_I(x_\delta)-\Phi_I(x^+)\le\delta obeys \[\|x_\delta-x^+\|\le\sqrt{2\delta/\sigma}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity converts an objective-accurate prox solve into an explicit distance-accurate prox point.
assumptions_latex: x_\delta\in Q has objective gap at most \delta.

notation.meaning: strong-convexity modulus of the prox geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Convexity Accuracy Conversion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical closed-form tractable prox mapping for simplex geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q=\Delta_n, h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\log x_i, and z\in\operatorname{ri}\Delta_n. Then the unique solution of \min_{x\in\Delta_n}\{\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_h(x,z)\} is \[x_i^+=\frac{z_i e^{-\eta g_i}}{\sum_{j=1}^n z_j e^{-\eta g_j}},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative-entropy geometry turns the simplex prox call into a normalized componentwise exponential update.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropic Simplex Prox Formula
Prox-Mapping Tractability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle condition for computationally accessible Bregman prox steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed convex set \(Q\), mirror function \(h\), center \(z\in Q\), dual vector \(g\), and stepsize \(\eta>0\), define the prox mapping by \[\operatorname{Prox}_{z}^{h}(\eta g)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\{\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_h(x,z)\}.\] The prox setup is tractable when this minimizer can be computed to the accuracy required by the outer method using an explicitly available finite procedure or oracle whose cost is controlled independently of solving the original optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prox setup is tractable when its Bregman-regularized linear minimization step can be computed efficiently to the required accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on the relevant domain.
\(\eta>0\) and \(g\) belongs to the dual space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Prox}_{z}^{h}(\eta g)\) is computationally accessible with a controlled per-call cost.

notation.meaning: Bregman prox mapping centered at z

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard oracle definition of prox-mapping tractability

children.title: Primal Prox Mirror Form
children.top_down_role: Mirror subgradient represented through a primal Bregman prox operation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Attainment Is Separate from Strong-Convexity Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence boundary for a primal Bregman-prox response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strong convexity of \(h\) makes \(x\mapsto\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_h(x,z)\) strongly convex and therefore gives at most one minimizer, but it does not ensure attainment on a nonclosed domain. For \(Q=(0,1)\), \(h(x)=x^2/2\), \(z=1/2\), and \(\eta g>1/2\), the infimum is approached at the excluded point \(0\), so the mirror response is undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity guarantees uniqueness only after existence; an open feasible domain can prevent attainment.
knowledge_statements.title: Attainment Is Separate from Strong-Convexity Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Invariance of the Mirror Generator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariance of the primal Bregman-prox response under affine perturbations of its generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\widetilde h(x)=h(x)+\langle a,x\rangle+c\), then \(D_{\widetilde h}(x,z)=D_h(x,z)\) wherever both divergences are defined. Hence \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\{\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_{\widetilde h}(x,z)\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\{\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_h(x,z)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding an affine function to a mirror generator changes neither its Bregman divergence nor its primal prox response.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable on the relevant mirror domain.
\(a\) is a dual vector and \(c\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_{\widetilde h}=D_h\quad\text{and the two argmin sets coincide}.

notation.meaning: affine perturbation of the mirror generator

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Invariance of the Mirror Generator
Primal Prox Mirror Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror subgradient iteration expressed as a primal Bregman prox minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_1\in Q\), stepsizes \(\eta_t>0\), and a differentiable strongly convex mirror function \(h\), at iteration \(t\) choose \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\) and compute \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}.\] Stop according to a prescribed iteration or accuracy rule and return either the final iterate or a specified weighted average of \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\). Strong convexity makes the displayed subproblem single-valued whenever a minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each mirror-subgradient step minimizes a linearized objective plus Bregman distance from the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on the convex feasible set \(Q\).
\(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on the prox domain.

notation.meaning: a convex subgradient of f at the current iterate

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and primal Bregman-prox update fit the leaf, and the mathematical formulation is standard. It nevertheless lacks the required inspectable source for the update, existence conditions, and output conventions.

children.title: Dual-Coordinate Mirror Form
children.top_down_role: Mirror subgradient represented through conjugate or dual coordinates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Reconstruction Requires Admissible Conjugate Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain boundary for the Legendre inverse-gradient formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The expression \(x_{t+1}=\nabla h^*(y_t-\eta_tg_t)\) requires \(y_t-\eta_tg_t\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h^*)\). If the translated coordinate leaves that domain, the displayed unconstrained mirror update is not defined without an alternative extension or a constrained prox formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The additive dual step must remain in the domain of the conjugate-gradient map.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Reconstruction Requires Admissible Conjugate Coordinates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-orthant specialization of the conjugate-coordinate form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\), let \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i\log x_i-x_i)\). Since \((\nabla h(x))_i=\log x_i\), the unconstrained dual-coordinate equation gives \[x_{t+1,i}=x_{t,i}\exp(-\eta_tg_{t,i}),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative-entropy geometry converts additive motion in log coordinates into a multiplicative primal update.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropy Coordinates Give Multiplicative Updates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Coordinates Recover Preconditioned Subgradient Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean specialization of the dual-coordinate mirror equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h(x)=\tfrac12\langle x,Mx\rangle\) with \(M\succ0\), \(\nabla h(x)=Mx\) and \(\nabla h^*(y)=M^{-1}y\). Hence \[x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_tM^{-1}g_t.\] In particular, \(M=I\) gives the ordinary unconstrained subgradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic mirror geometry turns the dual-coordinate update into a preconditioned subgradient step.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Coordinates Recover Preconditioned Subgradient Descent
Dual-Coordinate Mirror Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained Legendre mirror step written in gradient and conjugate coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be a Legendre convex function and suppose the iterates remain in \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\). For an unconstrained mirror-subgradient step with \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\) and \(\eta_t>0\), introduce \(y_t=\nabla h(x_t)\). The primal prox optimality equation is equivalent to \[y_{t+1}=y_t-\eta_t g_t,\qquad x_{t+1}=\nabla h^*(y_{t+1}).\] Thus the mirror step is additive in dual coordinates and is mapped back to the primal space through the gradient of the Fenchel conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In Legendre geometry, mirror descent subtracts the subgradient in dual coordinates and reconstructs the primal iterate through the conjugate gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is Legendre and \(h^*\) is its Fenchel conjugate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(
abla h(x_{t+1})=
abla h(x_t)-\eta_t g_t\) and \(x_{t+1}=
abla h^*(
abla h(x_t)-\eta_t g_t)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical Legendre-coordinate representation of mirror descent
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly targets the unconstrained dual-coordinate form, but the conjugate-gradient inverse relation requires precise Legendre-domain hypotheses and an authoritative source locator.

children.title: Constrained Mirror Subgradient
children.top_down_role: Mirror subgradient methods incorporating simple-set feasibility through prox access.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active Constraints Obstruct the Additive Dual Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between constrained mirror prox and the unconstrained dual-coordinate representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An exact constrained mirror step satisfies \[0\in\eta_tg_t+
abla h(x_{t+1})-
abla h(x_t)+N_Q(x_{t+1}).\] Unless a zero normal can satisfy this inclusion, it does not reduce to \(
abla h(x_{t+1})=
abla h(x_t)-\eta_tg_t\). Thus the unconstrained additive dual-coordinate formula is generally invalid when the constraint is active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active constraint contributes a normal-cone term, so constrained mirror descent is generally not a pure additive update in dual coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The convex first-order optimality condition applies to the attained prox subproblem.
\(h\) is differentiable at the relevant iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{an active normal-cone term may prevent }\nabla h(x_{t+1})=\nabla h(x_t)-\eta_tg_t.
knowledge_statements.title: Active Constraints Obstruct the Additive Dual Update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step inequality and ergodic guarantee for feasible Bregman prox steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(h\) is \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\), and let \[x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in Q}\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}.\] Then for every \(x\in Q\), \[\eta_t\langle g_t,x_t-x\rangle\le D_h(x,x_t)-D_h(x,x_{t+1})+\frac{\eta_t^2}{2\sigma}\|g_t\|_*^2.\] If \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), then for \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t)^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_tx_t\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x)\le\frac{D_h(x,x_1)+(2\sigma)^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t^2\|g_t\|_*^2}{\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained mirror step satisfies the telescoping Bregman inequality and the resulting feasible weighted-average objective bound.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex on the relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Mirror-Subgradient Fundamental Inequality
Constrained Mirror Subgradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror subgradient method enforcing simple-set feasibility through each prox subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be a nonempty closed convex set for which the Bregman prox mapping is available. Initialize \(x_1\in Q\). At iteration \(t\), obtain \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), choose \(\eta_t>0\), and set \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}.\] Every iterate is feasible. After \(T\) iterations, return \(x_T\) or the declared weighted average; convexity of \(Q\) ensures that any convexly weighted average of feasible iterates is also feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constrained method embeds feasibility in every Bregman prox step, so iterates and convexly weighted outputs remain in the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is strongly convex and its prox mapping over \(Q\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t\in Q\) for every generated iterate, and every convexly weighted output belongs to \(Q\).

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence defining the prox geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing the cumulative state by total weight gives a weighted mean with an exact one-step recursion.

Cumulative Subgradient State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit dual state formed by accumulating weighted subgradient observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given subgradients \(g_t\) and nonnegative oracle weights \(a_t\), initialize \(s_0=0\) in the dual space and update \[s_t=s_{t-1}+a_tg_t=\sum_{i=1}^{t}a_i g_i.\] The vector \(s_t\) is the cumulative subgradient state used by dual averaging. Its recursive update requires storing only the preceding state and the newest weighted subgradient, while preserving exactly the linear aggregate of all oracle information observed through iteration \(t\).

children.title: Regularized Primal Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of primal decisions from accumulated dual information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order certificate for the regularized primal response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H=h+\delta_Q\), a point \(x_{t+1}\) solves \(\min_x\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_tH(x)\}\) if and only if \[0\in s_t+\beta_t\partial H(x_{t+1}).\] When the convex subdifferential sum rule applies, this is equivalently \(0\in s_t+\beta_t\partial h(x_{t+1})+N_Q(x_{t+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reconstructed point is exact precisely when its regularizer subgradient and feasible-set normal balance the cumulative dual state.
knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Optimality Inclusion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity of the reconstructed point to perturbations of the cumulative state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(H=h+\delta_Q\) is \(\sigma\)-strongly convex and \(\beta>0\). If \(x(s)=\arg\min_x\{\langle s,x\rangle+\beta H(x)\}\), then \[\|x(s)-x(r)\|\le\frac{1}{\beta\sigma}\|s-r\|_*\] whenever both response problems attain their minima.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity makes the primal reconstruction single-valued and Lipschitz in the cumulative dual state.
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Stability of Primal Reconstruction
Regularized Primal Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal decision recovered from a cumulative dual state by regularized minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_t\) be a cumulative dual state, let \(Q\) be a closed convex feasible set, and let \(h:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) be strongly convex. For a scale \(\beta_t>0\), reconstruct the primal decision by \[x_{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}.\] The minimizer is unique whenever it exists. Equivalently, with \(H=h+\delta_Q\), the reconstruction satisfies \(x_{t+1}=\nabla H^*(-s_t/\beta_t)\) whenever \(H^*\) is differentiable at that point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal iterate is the unique regularized response to the accumulated dual subgradient state.
assumptions_latex: \(\beta_t>0\) and the reconstruction minimum is attained.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical guarantee for the baseline uniform-information variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\ge0\) be \(\sigma\)-strongly convex on \(Q\), let \(x_1\in\arg\min_Q h\), and fix \(\beta>0\). Generate \[x_t\in\arg\min_{x\in Q}\left\{\left\langle\sum_{i=1}^{t-1}g_i,x\right\rangle+\beta h(x)\right\}.\] If \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), then for every \(x\in Q\), \[\sum_{t=1}^T(f(x_t)-f(x))\le\beta h(x)+\frac{1}{2\sigma\beta}\sum_{t=1}^T\|g_t\|_*^2.\] Therefore, for \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^Tx_t\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x)\le\frac{\beta h(x)}{T}+\frac{1}{2\sigma\beta T}\sum_{t=1}^T\|g_t\|_*^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-scale regularized dual averaging has a regularizer-plus-squared-subgradient cumulative bound and the corresponding averaged objective guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Scale Uniform-Weight Dual-Averaging Bound
Regularized Dual Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual averaging with cumulative subgradients and a fixed prox regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_1\in Q\), a strongly convex regularizer \(h\), positive weights \(a_t\), and positive scales \(\beta_t\). Initialize \(s_0=0\). For \(t=1,\ldots,T\), obtain \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), set \(s_t=s_{t-1}+a_tg_t\), and compute \[x_{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}.\] Stop after \(T\) oracle calls and return the declared last iterate or weighted average. The regularizer converts the accumulated linear model into a well-defined primal response.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized dual averaging accumulates subgradients in a dual state and repeatedly minimizes their aggregate plus a strongly convex regularizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on the nonempty closed convex set \(Q\).
\(h\) is strongly convex and each reconstruction minimum is attained.

children.title: Weighted Dual Averaging
children.top_down_role: Dual averaging with nonuniform weighting of oracle information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical guarantee for nonuniform oracle weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\ge0\) be \(\sigma\)-strongly convex, fix \(\beta>0\), and define \(s_{t-1}=\sum_{i=1}^{t-1}a_i g_i\) and \[x_t\in\arg\min_{x\in Q}\{\langle s_{t-1},x\rangle+\beta h(x)\},\qquad a_t>0.\] If \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), then for every \(x\in Q\), \[\sum_{t=1}^Ta_t(f(x_t)-f(x))\le\beta h(x)+\frac{1}{2\sigma\beta}\sum_{t=1}^Ta_t^2\|g_t\|_*^2.\] Hence, for \(A_T=\sum_{t=1}^Ta_t\) and \(\bar x_T=A_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^Ta_tx_t\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x)\le\frac{\beta h(x)}{A_T}+\frac{\sum_{t=1}^Ta_t^2\|g_t\|_*^2}{2\sigma\beta A_T}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonuniform weights yield a weighted objective guarantee whose second-order term depends on squared weights.
assumptions_latex: \(a_t>0\), \(\beta>0\), and all reconstruction minima are attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Dual-Averaging Objective Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates relative observation weighting from an irrelevant common rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(c>0\), replacing \((a_1,\ldots,a_t,\beta)\) by \((ca_1,\ldots,ca_t,c\beta)\) multiplies the reconstruction objective by \(c\) and leaves its argmin unchanged. Thus exact reconstructed points depend on the ratios between observation weights and the regularization scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneously scaling all observation weights and regularization by the same positive factor does not change exact iterates.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Weight-Scale Invariance
Weighted Dual Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual averaging assigning nonuniform positive weights to oracle observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_t>0\) be prescribed, possibly nonuniform weights and set \(A_t=\sum_{i=1}^{t}a_i\). Starting from \(s_0=0\), obtain \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), update \(s_t=s_{t-1}+a_tg_t\), and reconstruct \[x_{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}.\] After \(T\) iterations, a canonical reported point is \(\bar x_T=A_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_t x_t\), although a declared last-iterate output may instead be used. Larger \(a_t\) gives the corresponding oracle observation proportionally greater influence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted dual averaging uses nonuniform weights in both the cumulative subgradient state and the canonical averaged output.

children.title: Adaptive-Regularization Dual Averaging
children.top_down_role: Dual averaging with an evolving regularization scale.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete nonanticipating adaptive regularization schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\beta_0>0\), define \[\beta_t=\sqrt{\beta_0^2+\sum_{i=1}^t a_i^2\|g_i\|_*^2}.\] After observing \(g_t\), update \(s_t=s_{t-1}+a_tg_t\) and set \[x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in Q}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}.\] The scale is positive, nondecreasing, and determined only by information available through iteration \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One adaptive variant scales regularization by the root cumulative squared norm of weighted subgradients.
assumptions_latex: \(\beta_0>0\), \(a_t>0\), and the observed dual norms are finite.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positivity Alone Gives No Adaptive Rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on claims for generic nonanticipating regularization scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conditions \(\beta_t>0\) and nonanticipation alone impose no quantitative relation between regularization and the observed subgradient magnitudes. They therefore do not imply a scale-adaptive regret or convergence bound without additional inequalities controlling the growth of \(\beta_t\) and terms such as \(a_t^2\|g_t\|_*^2/\beta_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrary positive nonanticipating scale is insufficient for an adaptive convergence guarantee.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptive Dual-Averaging Regret and Primal Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Potential bound for the accepted root-cumulative scale with each decision formed before the current oracle response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let h:Q\to\mathbb R_+ be 1-strongly convex with respect to \|\cdot\|, let \beta_0>0, and define s_t=\sum_{i=1}^t a_i g_i, q_t=a_t^2\|g_t\|_*^2, and \beta_t=(\beta_0^2+\sum_{i=1}^tq_i)^{1/2}. Choose x_1\in\arg\min_Qh and set x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in Q}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_th(x)\}. Then every u\in Q satisfies \[\sum_{t=1}^Ta_t\langle g_t,x_t-u\rangle\le\beta_Th(u)+\frac12\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{q_t}{\beta_{t-1}}.\] If g_t\in\partial f(x_t), A_T=\sum_{t=1}^Ta_t, and \bar x_T=A_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^Ta_tx_t, then \[f(\bar x_T)-f(u)\le\frac{\beta_Th(u)+\frac12\sum_{t=1}^Tq_t/\beta_{t-1}}{A_T}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root-cumulative regularization gives a timing-consistent comparator bound with previous-scale stability terms, which convex averaging converts into an objective guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Q is convex and every displayed reconstruction minimum is attained.
h\ge0 is 1-strongly convex with respect to \|\cdot\|.
For the objective conclusion, f is convex and g_t\in\partial f(x_t).

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative-Gradient Memory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted first-order information stored by dual averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(g_t\in E^*\) be the first-order vector observed at round \(t\), and let \(\eta_t>0\). The cumulative-gradient memory after round \(t\) is the dual vector \[s_t:=s_{t-1}+\eta_t g_t=\sum_{k=1}^{t}\eta_k g_k,\qquad s_0:=0.\] Thus the algorithm need not retain the individual vectors \(g_1,\ldots,g_t\); the single state \(s_t\) contains their weighted sum. Under the opposite sign convention, the stored state is \(-s_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative-gradient memory is the recursively maintained weighted sum of all previously observed first-order vectors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdifferential and Fenchel-conjugate characterizations of a cumulative-regularization response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_t:=\sum_{k=1}^t\eta_kg_k\) and \(\Phi_t:=R_t+\delta_X\). If \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\Phi_t(x)\},\] then \[0\in s_t+\partial\Phi_t(x_{t+1})\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x_{t+1}\in\partial\Phi_t^*(-s_t).\] If \(\Phi_t\) is strongly convex, the response is unique and equals \(\nabla\Phi_t^*(-s_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cumulative response has equivalent subgradient-inclusion and conjugate-response forms; strong convexity makes the response single-valued.
assumptions_latex: The response problem attains its minimum.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the constrained cumulative regularizer

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality and Conjugate Response Forms
Cumulative Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Follow-the-regularized-leader form with accumulated regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be nonempty and convex. Given linearized losses \(x\mapsto\langle g_k,x\rangle\) and proper convex regularizers \(r_k:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), define \[R_t(x):=\sum_{k=0}^{t}r_k(x).\] The cumulative-regularization response is \[x_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\sum_{k=1}^{t}\eta_k\langle g_k,x\rangle+R_t(x)\right\}.\] Consequently both information and geometry may accumulate over time: past gradients appear through their sum, while all regularization increments remain present through \(R_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative regularization chooses the next point by minimizing all past linearized losses plus the sum of regularizers introduced so far.
assumptions_latex: Each \(r_k\) is proper and convex, and the displayed problem attains a minimizer.

notation.meaning: regularization increment introduced at round k

children.title: Fixed Reference Geometry
children.top_down_role: Comparison regimes using a common reference geometry throughout the run.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scalar Rescaling Preserves the Reference Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between rescaling a fixed generator and inversely rescaling its learning-rate coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c>0\), \(D_{ch}(x,z)=cD_h(x,z)\), and therefore \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\eta\langle g,x\rangle+D_{ch}(x,z)\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{(\eta/c)\langle g,x\rangle+D_h(x,z)\}.\] Thus changing regularization strength by a scalar does not change the anisotropic reference geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scalar rescaling of a fixed generator is equivalent to inverse learning-rate rescaling, not directional geometry adaptation.
assumptions_latex: The displayed response problems are well-defined.

notation.meaning: positive scalar multiplier of the generator

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Rescaling Preserves the Reference Geometry
Fixed Reference Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-invariant mirror geometry with scalar step-size variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let one differentiable strongly convex function \(h:X\to\mathbb R\) be fixed before iteration. A fixed-reference mirror scheme uses the same divergence \(D_h\) at every round: \[x_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\bigl\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\bigr\}.\] Equivalently, a fixed-reference dual-averaging scheme may use \(x_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta_t h(x)\}\). The scalars \(\eta_t\) or \(\beta_t\) may vary, but the underlying distance-generating function and hence the anisotropic geometry do not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed reference geometry uses one distance-generating function throughout; step or regularization weights may vary without changing the underlying geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on its effective domain.
The displayed response problems attain minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{h_t}=D_h\) for every round when \(h_t=h\), while \(\eta_t\) and \(\beta_t\) may vary.

children.title: Adaptive Regularizer Geometry
children.top_down_role: Comparison regimes where regularization geometry varies with accumulated information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness boundary for unconstrained adaptive quadratic geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(H_t\succeq0\) is singular, \[\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+\tfrac12\|x-x_t\|_{H_t}^2\}\] is unbounded below when \(g_t\) has a nonzero component along \(\ker H_t\), and is nonunique when that component is zero. Positive curvature on every admissible direction, or constraints eliminating null-direction recession, is required for a unique response.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular adaptive metric can make the response unbounded or nonunique unless constraints or additional curvature control every null direction.
assumptions_latex: The response domain is the full ambient finite-dimensional vector space.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Adaptive Curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Shared Adaptivity Does Not Imply Mirror–FTRL Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on identifying adaptive mirror and cumulative-regularizer organizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Using history-dependent generators \(h_t\) in mirror descent and history-dependent cumulative regularizers \(R_t\) in FTRL does not by itself make their response sequences equal. Equality requires an explicit compatibility relation among the regularizers, initialization, indexing, and learning-rate conventions; absent such a relation, the two displays define distinct adaptive organizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive mirror descent and adaptive FTRL are not automatically equivalent merely because both vary their curvature over time.
assumptions_latex: Both schemes use causal, history-dependent regularization.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared Adaptivity Does Not Imply Mirror–FTRL Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic realization of adaptive mirror geometry by history-dependent positive-definite metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_t\succ0\) be selected from information available when \(x_{t+1}\) is formed and set \(h_t(x)=\tfrac12\langle x,H_tx\rangle\). Then \[D_{h_t}(x,z)=\tfrac12\|x-z\|_{H_t}^2,\qquad x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_tH_t^{-1}g_t\] for the unconstrained response. Thus changing curvature produces directional learning rates rather than only a scalar rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive quadratic regularizers act as variable metrics whose inverse curvature preconditions the current first-order vector.
assumptions_latex: \(H_t\) uses no information unavailable when \(x_{t+1}\) is selected.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Realization
Adaptive Regularizer Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round-dependent mirror geometry selected from observed information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_t:X\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and strongly convex, where \(h_t\) may depend only on information available through round \(t\). An adaptive-geometry mirror step is \[x_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\bigl\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_{h_t}(x,x_t)\bigr\}.\] In cumulative regularization, the same organization is expressed by \(R_t=R_{t-1}+r_t\) and \[x_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\bigl\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+R_t(x)\bigr\}.\] Adaptation changes directional curvature through \(h_t\) or \(R_t\), not merely through a scalar learning rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive regularizer geometry changes the round-dependent curvature using past information, allowing directional scaling beyond scalar step-size adjustment.
assumptions_latex: Each \(h_t\) is differentiable and strongly convex, or each cumulative \(R_t\) is strongly convex.
The chosen geometry is based only on information available by round \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\) is computed using the history-dependent geometry \(D_{h_t}\) or cumulative regularizer \(R_t\).

children.title: Online-Learning Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship to regret minimization and regularized leader methods.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Static Regret Does Not Control Unrestricted Dynamic Comparators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the fixed-comparator optimization correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A guarantee for \(\sum_{t=1}^T(f_t(x_t)-f_t(u))\) against every fixed \(u\in X\) does not by itself bound \(\sum_{t=1}^T(f_t(x_t)-f_t(u_t))\) for an unrestricted changing comparator sequence. Dynamic-regret conclusions require additional comparator-variation control and a corresponding algorithmic bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static regret supports comparison with one fixed point, not an unrestricted comparator that changes each round.
assumptions_latex: The available guarantee is only static regret against fixed comparators.
knowledge_statements.title: Static Regret Does Not Control Unrestricted Dynamic Comparators

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Online-to-Batch Conversion for a Repeated Convex Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of static regret into an averaged optimization guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be convex and suppose \[\operatorname{Reg}_T(u):=\sum_{t=1}^T(f(x_t)-f(u))\le B_T.\] Then \(\bar x_T:=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T x_t\in X\) and \[f(\bar x_T)-f(u)\le B_T/T.\] More generally, positive weights \(w_t\) give the same conclusion with \(\bar x_T=\sum_tw_tx_t/\sum_tw_t\) and the weighted regret divided by \(\sum_tw_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static regret for repeated use of one convex objective becomes an objective-gap bound for the averaged decisions.
assumptions_latex: The stated static-regret bound holds for the comparator \(u\).
knowledge_statements.title: Online-to-Batch Conversion for a Repeated Convex Objective
Online-Learning Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order optimization viewed as online linear-loss minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex losses \(f_t:X\to\mathbb R\), choose \(g_t\in\partial f_t(x_t)\) and define the online linear loss \(\ell_t(x):=\langle g_t,x\rangle\). Mirror descent is online mirror descent applied to \(\ell_t\), while dual averaging is follow-the-regularized-leader applied to their weighted sum: \[x_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\sum_{k=1}^{t}\eta_k\ell_k(x)+R_t(x)\right\}.\] Moreover, for every \(u\in X\), convexity gives \[f_t(x_t)-f_t(u)\le\ell_t(x_t)-\ell_t(u).\] Thus a regret bound for the linear losses yields the corresponding cumulative optimization-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subgradients define online linear losses; mirror descent and dual averaging become online mirror descent and regularized leader methods, whose regret controls optimization error.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is convex and each \(f_t\) is convex on \(X\).
The regularized-leader subproblem attains a minimizer.

notation.meaning: linear loss induced by the observed subgradient
regularizer used by the leader response
