children.title: Objective–Constraint Switching Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods switching information channels according to current feasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Productive Iterates Need Not Exist Under Arbitrary Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output failure for an underspecified productive-versus-restoration switching method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), let \(g(x)=|x|\le0\), start at \(x_0=\tfrac12\), and use the restoration step \(x_{t+1}=x_t-d_t\) with \(d_t=\operatorname{sign}(x_t)\). Then \(x_t\in\{\tfrac12,-\tfrac12\}\) for every t, so the productive set \(I_T=\{t<T:g(x_t)\le0\}\) is empty for every horizon T. A designated productive iterate and an average normalized over \(I_T\) are therefore undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a stepsize or progress condition, a feasible switching problem can generate no productive iterates, making productive-only output rules undefined.
assumptions_latex: The switching rule permits arbitrary positive restoration steps.
The output is required to use productive iterates only.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility alone does not guarantee \(I_T\ne\varnothing\); the output rule must handle the empty case or impose conditions excluding it.

notation.meaning: Productive iteration indices before horizon T.

knowledge_statements.title: Productive Iterates Need Not Exist Under Arbitrary Steps

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fully specified projected switching method with a nonempty productive output and simultaneous objective-feasibility guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}g_i(x)\), let \(x^*\in X\) satisfy \(g(x^*)\le0\), and suppose \(\|x_0-x^*\|\le R\), where \(R>0\). For a horizon \(T\ge1\), set \(\alpha=R/(G\sqrt T)\) and \(\varepsilon=RG/\sqrt T\). Assume every selected objective or active-constraint subgradient has norm at most \(G>0\). If \(g(x_k)\le\varepsilon\), choose \(d_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) and declare \(k\) productive; otherwise choose \(i_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_i g_i(x_k)\) and \(d_k\in\partial g_{i_k}(x_k)\). Set \(x_{k+1}=P_X(x_k-\alpha d_k)\). Then \(I_T=\{k<T:g(x_k)\le\varepsilon\}\) is nonempty, and \(\bar x_T=|I_T|^{-1}\sum_{k\in I_T}x_k\) satisfies \[g(\bar x_T)\le\frac{RG}{\sqrt T},\qquad f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{RG}{\sqrt T}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A horizon-calibrated switching rule produces productive iterates whose average has objective error and maximum constraint violation at most RG divided by square root T.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are convex on \(X\).
Every branch-selected subgradient has norm at most \(G>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I_T\ne\varnothing,\quad f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le RG/\sqrt T,\quad \max_i g_i(\bar x_T)\le RG/\sqrt T.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Productive-Iterate Switching Guarantee
Objective–Constraint Switching Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient switching for convex functional constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) over \(X\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Fix tolerances \(\varepsilon_t\ge0\), steps \(\alpha_t>0\), and initialize \(x_1\in X\). At round \(t\), if \(G(x_t):=\max_i g_i(x_t)\le\varepsilon_t\), choose \(d_t\in\partial f(x_t)\); otherwise choose an active index \(i_t\in\mathop{\rm argmax}_i g_i(x_t)\) and \(d_t\in\partial g_{i_t}(x_t)\). Update \[x_{t+1}=P_X(x_t-\alpha_td_t).\] Return a designated feasible productive iterate or an average of productive iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method takes objective steps at sufficiently feasible iterates and active-constraint restoration steps otherwise, followed by projection onto the simple domain.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are proper convex functions with available subgradients.
Each active branch supplies a finite subgradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}=P_X(x_t-\alpha_td_t)\), with \(d_t\) selected from the objective or a maximally violated constraint according to feasibility.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard productive-versus-nonproductive projected subgradient switching scheme
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Penalty Subgradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Subgradient methods applied through nonsmooth penalty reformulations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient descent on a convex maximum-violation penalty reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le 0\), define \(V(x)=\max\{0,g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x)\}\) and \(F_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V(x)\). Starting from \(x_0\in X\), choose \(v_t\in\partial F_\rho(x_t)\) and set \[x_{t+1}=P_X(x_t-\alpha_t v_t),\qquad \alpha_t>0.\] Under the convex subdifferential sum and maximum rules, one may choose \(v_t=u_t+\rho z_t\), where \(u_t\in\partial f(x_t)\) and \(z_t\) is a convex combination of subgradients of the active functions among \(0,g_1,\ldots,g_m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method applies projected subgradient descent to the objective plus a maximum positive constraint-violation penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are proper convex functions and the stated subdifferential rules apply at the iterates.
\(\rho>0\), \(\alpha_t>0\), and the required subgradients and projection are available.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the base set.

review_flags: Corrects the malformed assumptions and ambiguous output rule in the deferred seed.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Penalty Subgradient Iteration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected-subgradient convergence for a fixed convex penalty objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_\rho^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F_\rho(x)\), and generate \(x_{t+1}=P_X(x_t-\alpha_t v_t)\), where \(v_t\in\partial F_\rho(x_t)\), \(\|v_t\|_2\le L_\rho\), and \(\alpha_t>0\). Then, for every \(T\ge1\), \[\min_{0\le t<T}\bigl(F_\rho(x_t)-F_\rho(x_\rho^*)\bigr)\le\frac{\|x_0-x_\rho^*\|_2^2+L_\rho^2\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\alpha_t^2}{2\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\alpha_t}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard projected-subgradient best-iterate bound applies directly to the fixed penalized objective.
assumptions_latex: \(F_\rho\) is convex and attains its minimum on \(X\).
The selected penalized subgradients satisfy \(\|v_t\|_2\le L_\rho\), and \(\alpha_t>0\).

notation.meaning: Uniform bound on selected penalized subgradient norms.
Minimum penalized objective value over the base set.

review_flags: Removed the builder's extraneous asymptotic exactness sentence from this finite-horizon claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Penalized Best-Iterate Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar boundary example for the maximum-violation penalty coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{-x:x\le0\}\), the unique primal solution is \(x^*=0\), an optimal multiplier is \(\lambda^*=1\), and \(F_\rho(x)=-x+\rho[x]_+\). If \(\rho<1\), then \(\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}F_\rho(x)=-\infty\). If \(\rho=1\), every \(x\ge0\) minimizes \(F_\rho\), including infeasible points. If \(\rho>1\), the unique penalized minimizer is \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the multiplier threshold the penalty can be unbounded, and equality need not exclude infeasible minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb R\), \(f(x)=-x\), and the sole constraint is \(g(x)=x\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho<\|\lambda^*\|_1\) may destroy boundedness, while equality need not make every penalized minimizer feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Exact-Penalty Threshold

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global exactness under an attained optimal Lagrange-multiplier certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^*=\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ g_i(x)\le0\}\). Suppose \(x^*\) is primal optimal and \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R_+^m\) is dual optimal with \(q(\lambda^*)=p^*\). For \(V(x)=\max\{0,g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x)\}\) and \(F_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V(x)\), if \(\rho\ge\|\lambda^*\|_1\), then \(F_\rho(x)\ge p^*\) for every \(x\in X\), every primal solution minimizes \(F_\rho\), and \(\min_XF_\rho=p^*\). If \(\rho>\|\lambda^*\|_1\), every attained minimizer of \(F_\rho\) is feasible and primal optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum-violation penalty is exact at the one-norm of an optimal multiplier, while strict domination guarantees feasibility of every penalized minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and convex, and \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are convex on \(X\).
The primal optimum is attained and there is a dual-optimal multiplier \(\lambda^*\ge0\) satisfying \(q(\lambda^*)=p^*\).
Existence of a penalized minimizer is assumed when conclusions about every such minimizer are invoked.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Threshold for Maximum-Violation Penalization
Penalty Subgradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient descent on a convex hinge-penalty reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex program \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\), define \[F_\rho(x):=f(x)+\rho\,[G(x)]_+,\qquad G(x):=\max_{1\le i\le m}g_i(x),\] where \(\rho>0\). Initialize \(x_1\in X\). At round \(t\), select \(v_t\in\partial F_\rho(x_t)\) and update \[x_{t+1}=P_X(x_t-\alpha_tv_t),\qquad \alpha_t>0.\] If \(G(x_t)<0\), one may take \(v_t\in\partial f(x_t)\); if \(G(x_t)>0\), one may add \(\rho\) times a convex combination of subgradients of maximally violated constraints. Return the prescribed last, best, or averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty subgradient method applies projected subgradient descent to the objective plus a positive-part penalty on maximum constraint violation.

children.title: Target-Level Control
children.top_down_role: Constraint-handling policies organized around prescribed objective or constraint levels.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested Target-Feasible Sets and the Optimal Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural dependence of level-feasibility systems on the prescribed objective target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L\in\mathbb R\), define \[S_L=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ f(x)\le L\}.\] If \(L_1\le L_2\), then \(S_{L_1}\subseteq S_{L_2}\). If the original feasible set is nonempty and \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g_i(x)\le0\}\) is finite, then \[p^*=\inf\{L\in\mathbb R:S_L\ne\varnothing\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Target-feasible sets expand monotonically with the target, and their feasibility threshold is the primal optimal value.
assumptions_latex: The original constraint-feasible set is nonempty.
The primal optimal infimum is finite.

notation.meaning: Constraint-feasible set augmented by objective target L.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Target-Feasible Sets and the Optimal Threshold
Target-Level Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level feasibility for a prescribed objective target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a target level \(L\in\mathbb R\), convert the constrained objective system into \[f(x)\le L,\qquad g_i(x)\le0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\] and define \(\Phi_L(x):=\max\{f(x)-L,g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x)\}\). Initialize \(x_1\in X\). While \(\Phi_L(x_t)>\varepsilon\), choose an active function \(q_t\in\{f-L,g_1,\ldots,g_m\}\), take \(d_t\in\partial q_t(x_t)\), and set \[x_{t+1}=P_X(x_t-\alpha_td_t).\] Stop with an \(\varepsilon\)-level-feasible point when \(\Phi_L(x_t)\le\varepsilon\); otherwise apply the prescribed budget rule and revise the target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Target-level control treats the objective bound as another convex inequality and reduces the largest objective-or-constraint violation by projected subgradient steps.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,ots,g_m\) are proper convex functions with available active subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stopping test \(\Phi_L(x_t)\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(f(x_t)\le L+\varepsilon\) and \(g_i(x_t)\le\varepsilon\) for every \(i\).

children.title: Feasibility-Restoration Control
children.top_down_role: Policies prioritizing recovery of acceptable constraint violation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restoration Complexity for a Positive Feasibility Tolerance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-only maximum-violation restoration with bounded subgradients and a planned constant stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(x)=\max_i g_i(x)\), choose \(i_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_i g_i(x_t)\), \(d_t\in\partial g_{i_t}(x_t)\), and set \(x_{t+1}=P_X(x_t-\alpha d_t)\). Suppose \(\bar x\in X\) satisfies \(g_i(\bar x)\le0\) for every i, \(\|x_0-\bar x\|\le D\), and \(\|d_t\|\le M\). For a horizon \(T\ge1\), taking \(\alpha=D/(M\sqrt T)\) gives \[\min_{0\le t<T}G(x_t)\le \frac{DM}{\sqrt T}.\] Hence for \(\varepsilon>0\), restoration reaches \(G(x_t)\le\varepsilon\) within any horizon satisfying \(T\ge(DM/\varepsilon)^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a feasible comparator, bounded constraint subgradients, and a calibrated constant step, restoration finds an epsilon-feasible iterate in order epsilon to the minus two steps.
assumptions_latex: A feasible comparator \(\bar x\in X\) exists.
\(\|x_0-\bar x\|\le D\) and selected restoration subgradients have norm at most \(M>0\).
The horizon-based constant stepsize is \(D/(M\sqrt T)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{0\le t<T}G(x_t)\le DM/\sqrt T\), yielding \(O((DM/\varepsilon)^2)\) restoration complexity for \(\varepsilon>0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projected-subgradient distance estimate against a feasible comparator

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Steps Do Not Guarantee Restoration Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp one-dimensional failure of an unqualified constraint-only restoration loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), \(g(x)=|x|\), and require \(g(x)\le0\). With \(x_0=\tfrac12\), \(\varepsilon=0\), \(\alpha_t=1\), and \(d_t=\operatorname{sign}(x_t)\in\partial g(x_t)\), the update \(x_{t+1}=x_t-d_t\) alternates between \(\tfrac12\) and \(-\tfrac12\). Thus \(g(x_t)=\tfrac12\) for every t despite the nonempty feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary positive restoration steps can cycle forever even for one convex constraint with a nonempty feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The restoration update permits arbitrary positive unnormalized steps.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive stepsizes alone imply neither convergence to feasibility nor finite termination.

Feasibility-Restoration Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-only restoration phase for infeasible iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(x):=\max_{1\le i\le m}g_i(x)\) for convex constraints \(g_i(x)\le0\) on a closed convex set \(X\). Given an infeasible iterate \(x_t\) with \(G(x_t)>\varepsilon\), choose \(i_t\in\mathop{\rm argmax}_i g_i(x_t)\), select \(d_t\in\partial g_{i_t}(x_t)\), and perform \[x_{t+1}=P_X(x_t-\alpha_td_t),\qquad \alpha_t>0.\] Repeat constraint steps without using an objective subgradient until \(G(x_t)\le\varepsilon\), then return control to the objective or target-level phase. The restoration stopping test certifies componentwise \(\varepsilon\)-feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an iterate is infeasible, restoration temporarily ignores the objective and takes projected subgradient steps against a maximally violated constraint.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) is proper and convex with an available subgradient at restoration iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(x_t)\le\varepsilon\) at restoration termination, hence \(g_i(x_t)\le\varepsilon\) for all \(i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected maximum-residual switching for a feasible fixed target with bounded branch subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply the switching update to \(Q_\ell=\max_i h_i\). Suppose a target-feasible point \(\bar x\in X\) exists, so \(Q_\ell(\bar x)\le0\), and suppose \(\|x_0-\bar x\|\le D\) and every selected active-branch subgradient has norm at most \(M\). For a horizon \(T\), choose \(\alpha=D/(M\sqrt T)\). Then \[\min_{0\le k<T}Q_\ell(x^k)\le\frac{DM}{\sqrt T}.\] Consequently an \(\varepsilon\)-level-feasible iterate is obtained within \(T\ge(DM/\varepsilon)^2\) iterations for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible target, bounded active-branch subgradients and a calibrated constant step give the standard inverse-square epsilon complexity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp infeasibility boundary for targets strictly below an attained convex program optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_\ell(x)=\max\{f(x)-\ell,g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x)\}\). If \(\ell<p^*\), then \(\{x\in X:Q_\ell(x)\leq0\}=\varnothing\). assumptions_latex: The target satisfies \(\ell<p^*\), where \(p^*=\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ g_i(x)\leq0\ \forall i\}\) is finite.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Forms for Standard Multiplier Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projections for sign, box, affine, and conic multiplier domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z\in\mathbb R^d\), \[(P_{\mathbb R_+^d}z)_i=\max\{z_i,0\},\qquad (P_{[\ell,u]}z)_i=\min\{u_i,\max\{\ell_i,z_i\}\}.\] If \(\Lambda=\{y:By=c\}\) and \(B\) has full row rank, then \[P_\Lambda z=z-B^{\mathsf T}(BB^{\mathsf T})^{-1}(Bz-c).\] For a nonempty closed convex cone \(K\), \[z=P_Kz+P_{K^\circ}z,\qquad \langle P_Kz,P_{K^\circ}z\rangle=0,\] where \(K^\circ=\{w:\langle w,k\rangle\le0\ \forall k\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthant and box projections clip coordinates, affine projections remove the row-space residual, and cone projections satisfy Moreau decomposition.

\(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.

Known Lower-Bound Gap Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certifies objective suboptimality from a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) have optimal value \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\), and suppose a known scalar \(L\) satisfies \(L\leq f^*\). For any candidate \(\hat x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\), define \[G_L(\hat x):=f(\hat x)-L.\] Then \(f(\hat x)-f^*\leq G_L(\hat x)\). Hence the directly verifiable inequality \(G_L(\hat x)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(f(\hat x)-f^*\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a valid global lower bound from the candidate value gives a computable upper bound on objective suboptimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Supporting-Model Gap Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses accumulated subgradient affine minorants to construct a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, and let \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) for \(i=0,\ldots,T-1\). Define \[m_T(x):=\max_{0\leq i<T}\{f(x_i)+\langle g_i,x-x_i\rangle\},\qquad L_T:=\inf_{x\in C}m_T(x).\] The subgradient inequality gives \(m_T(x)\leq f(x)\) on \(C\), hence \(L_T\leq f^*:=\inf_C f\). For any \(\hat x\in C\), \(G_T:=f(\hat x)-L_T\) satisfies \(f(\hat x)-f^*\leq G_T\); thus \(G_T\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of collected affine minorants yields a global lower bound, whose gap to the candidate value certifies suboptimality.

Target-Level Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assesses attainment relative to a prescribed objective target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), let \(\ell\in\mathbb{R}\) be a prescribed target level, and let \(\hat x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\). The computable residual is \[R_\ell(\hat x):=[f(\hat x)-\ell]_+.\] The condition \(R_\ell(\hat x)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies target attainment \(f(\hat x)\leq\ell+\varepsilon\). If additionally \(\ell\leq f^*:=\inf_C f\), it also certifies \(f(\hat x)-f^*\leq\varepsilon\). Without the lower-bound condition, target attainment alone is not an optimality certificate.

children.title: Primal–Dual Certificate
children.top_down_role: Joint quality assessment from primal recovery and dual bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Sided Decomposition of the Primal–Dual Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The same gap bounds both primal and dual value errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For primal-feasible \(\hat x\) and \(\hat\lambda\ge0\), weak duality gives \(d(\hat\lambda)\le p^*\le f_0(\hat x)\), and \[G_{\mathrm{pd}}(\hat x,\hat\lambda)=f_0(\hat x)-d(\hat\lambda)=\bigl(f_0(\hat x)-p^*\bigr)+\bigl(p^*-d(\hat\lambda)\bigr).\] Both terms are nonnegative. Thus \(G_{\mathrm{pd}}\le\varepsilon\) bounds both errors by \(\varepsilon\), while \(G_{\mathrm{pd}}=0\) certifies equality of the primal value, dual value, and optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual gap is the sum of primal and dual value errors, so it bounds both; zero gap certifies optimality on both sides.
assumptions_latex: The primal optimal value is finite.

notation.meaning: primal feasible value minus Lagrangian dual value

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Decomposition of the Primal–Dual Gap
Primal–Dual Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses weak duality to certify a feasible primal candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex problem \(p^*:=\inf\{f_0(x):x\in X,\ f_j(x)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), define \(L(x,\lambda):=f_0(x)+\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jf_j(x)\) and \(d(\lambda):=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)\). If \(\hat x\) is primal feasible and \(\hat\lambda\geq0\), weak duality gives \(d(\hat\lambda)\leq p^*\leq f_0(\hat x)\). Therefore \[G_{\mathrm{pd}}(\hat x,\hat\lambda):=f_0(\hat x)-d(\hat\lambda)\] is nonnegative and upper-bounds primal suboptimality. The condition \(G_{\mathrm{pd}}\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(f_0(\hat x)-p^*\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal value minus a dual lower bound is a computable upper bound on primal suboptimality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Potential Need Not Decrease Every Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on treating squared distance as a monotone Lyapunov function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The basic recursion gives the sufficient monotonicity condition \[2(f(x_t)-f(u))\ge\alpha_t\|g_t\|_2^2.\] More generally, the retained projection-residual term can compensate when this condition fails. Without such control, convexity alone does not guarantee \(\|x_{t+1}-u\|_2\le\|x_t-u\|_2\) for arbitrary positive stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared distance is a comparison potential, but a large step can make it increase on an individual iteration.
assumptions_latex: The projected-subgradient recursion of the deferred seed holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Potential Need Not Decrease Every Iteration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharper Euclidean potential inequality retaining projection decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_t=x_t-\alpha_tg_t\) and \(x_{t+1}=\Pi_C(z_t)\). For every \(u\in C\), \[\|x_{t+1}-u\|_2^2\le\|x_t-u\|_2^2-2\alpha_t\langle g_t,x_t-u\rangle+\alpha_t^2\|g_t\|_2^2-\|z_t-x_{t+1}\|_2^2.\] If \(f\) is convex, the inner product may be lower-bounded by \(f(x_t)-f(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection contributes an additional nonnegative residual decrease beyond the usual subgradient recursion.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Residual Strengthening
Euclidean Distance Potential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step projected-subgradient potential inequality in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, let \(f\) be convex, and update \(x_{t+1}:=\Pi_C(x_t-\alpha_tg_t)\) with \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\) and \(\alpha_t\geq0\). For any comparator \(u\in C\), projection nonexpansiveness and the subgradient inequality yield \[\|x_{t+1}-u\|_2^2\leq\|x_t-u\|_2^2-2\alpha_t\bigl(f(x_t)-f(u)\bigr)+\alpha_t^2\|g_t\|_2^2.\] Thus squared distance to a minimizer is a potential whose decrease controls the objective gap up to the stepsize-squared error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared Euclidean distance decreases by twice the stepsize times the objective gap, up to a squared-subgradient error term.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a neighborhood of \(C\)

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the constraint set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projected-subgradient recursion is correct and fits a Euclidean potential principle, but the record lacks a source with a specific theorem, section, or page locator.

children.title: Bregman Divergence Potential
children.top_down_role: Divergence-to-comparator organization for mirror analysis.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bregman Divergence Is Not Generally a Metric
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting the directed mirror potential as a distance metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Convexity and strong convexity do not generally imply \(D_h(u,x)=D_h(x,u)\), and Bregman divergence need not satisfy the triangle inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman divergence is a directed potential and generally is not a metric.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and convex on its domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_h\text{ need not be symmetric or satisfy the triangle inequality}
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Divergence Is Not Generally a Metric

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-distance lower bound supplied by the mirror map's strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(h\) is \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\), then \[D_h(u,x)\ge\frac{\sigma}{2}\|u-x\|^2\ge0.\] In particular, \(D_h(u,x)=0\) implies \(u=x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strongly convex mirror map makes its Bregman potential nonnegative and controlling of squared norm distance.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Convexity Control of Bregman Divergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identity underlying comparator-potential changes in mirror analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For differentiable \(h\) and admissible \(u,x,y\), \[\langle\nabla h(y)-\nabla h(x),u-y\rangle=D_h(u,x)-D_h(u,y)-D_h(y,x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mirror-gradient difference equals the change in comparator divergence minus the step divergence.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable at \(x\) and \(y\), and all displayed divergences are finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Three-Point Identity
Bregman Divergence Potential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step mirror-subgradient potential inequality relative to a comparator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex on a convex set \(C\) with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\), and define \(D_h(u,x):=h(u)-h(x)-\langle\nabla h(x),u-x\rangle\). For \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), let \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{\alpha_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\}.\] Then every \(u\in C\) satisfies \[\alpha_t(f(x_t)-f(u))\leq D_h(u,x_t)-D_h(u,x_{t+1})+\frac{\alpha_t^2}{2\sigma}\|g_t\|_*^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman divergence telescopes under a mirror-subgradient step and controls the objective gap up to a dual-norm error.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha_t\geq0\) and the mirror update has a solution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mirror-step Bregman potential inequality is standard and correctly placed, but its hypotheses and constant require an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Telescoping-Averaging Analysis Principles
children.top_down_role: Potential aggregation mechanisms connecting trajectories to reported outputs.

children.title: Potential Telescoping
children.top_down_role: Aggregation of consecutive potential comparisons across a trajectory.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sign-Free Telescoping and the Terminal-Potential Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates algebraic cancellation from the lower bound needed to discard the terminal potential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For arbitrary real \(a_t,\Delta_t,b_t,V_t\), inequalities \(V_{t+1}\leq V_t-a_t\Delta_t+b_t\) imply \[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}a_t\Delta_t\leq V_0-V_T+\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}b_t.\] Thus neither \(a_t\geq0\) nor \(V_t\geq0\) is needed for cancellation itself. If only \(V_T\geq L\) is known, then \[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}a_t\Delta_t\leq V_0-L+\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}b_t.\] Without a finite lower bound on \(V_T\), the terminal term cannot be uniformly discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Telescoping is sign-free algebra; only the simplified bound that removes the terminal potential requires a known terminal lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(V_T\geq L\) only when the terminal term is to be discarded

notation.meaning: known lower bound for the terminal potential

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Free Telescoping and the Terminal-Potential Boundary
Potential Telescoping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summation rule converting one-step potential decrease into cumulative progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_t\geq0\), \(a_t\geq0\), and suppose a one-step analysis gives \[V_{t+1}\leq V_t-a_t\Delta_t+b_t\qquad(t=0,\ldots,T-1).\] Summing and canceling intermediate potentials yields \[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}a_t\Delta_t\leq V_0-V_T+\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}b_t\leq V_0+\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}b_t.\] When \(\Delta_t=f(x_t)-f(u)\), this inequality supplies the cumulative objective-gap bound used by averaging and best-iterate extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing one-step potential inequalities cancels intermediate potentials and bounds accumulated progress by the initial potential plus accumulated errors.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic telescoping of one-step inequalities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The telescoping principle is algebraically correct and matches the leaf, but no cited source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Uniform Output Averaging
children.top_down_role: Trajectory aggregation using equal iterate weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Output Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts an unweighted cumulative gap bound into an averaged-output guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be convex, let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, and define the uniform average \[\bar x_T:=\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}x_t.\] For any comparator \(u\in C\), convexity gives \[f(\bar x_T)-f(u)\leq\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\bigl(f(x_t)-f(u)\bigr).\] Therefore, whenever a potential argument establishes \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}(f(x_t)-f(u))\leq B_T\), the reported average satisfies \(f(\bar x_T)-f(u)\leq B_T/T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity transfers an unweighted cumulative objective-gap bound to the arithmetic mean of the iterates.

notation.meaning: uniform average of the first T iterates

source_refs.locator: A. Convex Sets and Functions p. 38

source_witnesses.locator: A. Convex Sets and Functions p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity Boundaries for Uniform Output Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates domain feasibility from the convex-objective Jensen guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Uniform averaging requires a convex domain to preserve feasibility and a convex objective for Jensen transfer. If \(C=\{-1,1\}\), then the average of \(-1\) and \(1\) is \(0\notin C\). Even on the convex domain \([-1,1]\), the nonconvex function \(f(x)=-x^2\) with \(x_0=-1\), \(x_1=1\) satisfies \(\bar x_2=0\) but \(f(\bar x_2)=0>-1=(f(x_0)+f(x_1))/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex domain is needed for feasibility of the arithmetic mean, and a convex objective is needed to transfer the average objective bound.
assumptions_latex: The first example removes domain convexity
The second example removes objective convexity
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x_T\in C\) or \(f(\bar x_T)\leq T^{-1}\sum_tf(x_t)\) may fail when the respective convexity assumption is omitted
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity Boundaries for Uniform Output Averaging

children.title: Stepsize-Weighted Averaging
children.top_down_role: Trajectory aggregation using weights derived from the selected step scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Stepsize-Weighted Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts a stepsize-weighted cumulative gap into a weighted-output guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be convex, let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, and let \(\alpha_t\geq0\) with \(A_T:=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\alpha_t>0\). Define \[\bar x_T^{\alpha}:=\frac1{A_T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\alpha_tx_t.\] For every \(u\in C\), convexity yields \[f(\bar x_T^{\alpha})-f(u)\leq\frac1{A_T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\alpha_t\bigl(f(x_t)-f(u)\bigr).\] Thus a bound \(\sum_t\alpha_t(f(x_t)-f(u))\leq B_T\) implies \(f(\bar x_T^{\alpha})-f(u)\leq B_T/A_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity transfers a stepsize-weighted cumulative gap bound to the corresponding weighted average of iterates.

source_refs.locator: A. Convex Sets and Functions p. 38

source_witnesses.locator: A. Convex Sets and Functions p. 38

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp weight-sign and domain-convexity requirements for feasibility and Jensen transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The output \(\bar x_T^\alpha=A_T^{-1}\sum_t\alpha_tx_t\) is guaranteed to lie in \(C\) and satisfy Jensen's inequality when \(\alpha_t\geq0\), \(A_T>0\), and \(C\) is convex. Both structural conditions matter. With \(C=[0,1]\), \(x_0=0\), \(x_1=1\), \(\alpha_0=-1\), and \(\alpha_1=2\), one has \(A_T=1\) but \(\bar x_T^\alpha=2\notin C\). With the nonconvex set \(C=\{-1,1\}\), equal positive weights give \(\bar x=0\notin C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative normalized weights and a convex domain are both necessary for universal feasibility of the weighted output; convexity of the objective is additionally required for Jensen transfer.
assumptions_latex: The counterexamples separately remove weight nonnegativity or domain convexity
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x_T^\alpha\in C\) is not guaranteed if signed weights are allowed or \(C\) is nonconvex
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Combination Boundaries for Stepsize Averaging

children.title: Best-Iterate Extraction
children.top_down_role: Selection-based conversion from trajectory information to reported objective quality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp sign boundary for extracting a best observed value from a weighted cumulative bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(A:=\sum_t a_t>0\). The inequality \(\min_t q_t\leq A^{-1}\sum_ta_tq_t\) holds for every real vector \((q_t)\) if and only if every \(a_t\geq0\). With signed weights it can fail: \(a_0=2\), \(a_1=-1\), \(q_0=1\), and \(q_1=2\) give \(A=1\) but \(A^{-1}\sum_ta_tq_t=0<1=\min_tq_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive total weight is insufficient: universal best-iterate extraction requires every weight to be nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_tq_t\leq A^{-1}\sum_ta_tq_t\text{ for all }(q_t)\iff a_t\geq0\text{ for all }t\)
knowledge_statements.title: Necessity of Nonnegative Extraction Weights
Best-Iterate Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extracts an individual iterate from a weighted cumulative objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_t\geq0\) with \(A_T:=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}a_t>0\). For any real values \(q_t\), \[\min_{0\leq t<T}q_t\leq\frac1{A_T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}a_tq_t.\] Taking \(q_t=f(x_t)-f(u)\), any bound \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}a_t(f(x_t)-f(u))\leq B_T\) implies \[\min_{0\leq t<T}f(x_t)-f(u)\leq\frac{B_T}{A_T}.\] Hence an index \(t_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\leq t<T}f(x_t)\) provides an individual iterate with the stated guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted average gap bounds the smallest observed gap, so selecting the best objective value yields an individual guaranteed iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x_t)\) is finite for every considered iterate

notation.meaning: index of a smallest observed objective value

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimum does not exceed a convex combination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The best-iterate extraction property is correct for nonnegative weights of positive total mass and fits the leaf, but it lacks an inspectable source citation.

children.title: General Convex Subgradient Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Baseline convergence families for Lipschitz nonsmooth convex objectives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Best-Iterate Bound for Diminishing-Step Subgradient Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-time objective-gap guarantee for Euclidean subgradient iterations on a Lipschitz convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and \(B\)-Lipschitz continuous, and suppose it admits a minimizer \(\eta_*\) satisfying \(\|\eta_* - \theta_0\|_2\leq D\). For subgradient-method iterates generated with \(\gamma_t=D/(B\sqrt{t})\), every integer \(t\geq1\) satisfies \[\min_{0\leq s\leq t-1}\bigl(F(\theta_s)-F(\eta_*)\bigr)\leq DB\frac{2+\log t}{2\sqrt{t}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex B-Lipschitz objective having a minimizer within Euclidean distance D of the initial point, the subgradient method with step size D divided by B times the square root of t attains a best-iterate objective gap no greater than DB(2 + log t)/(2 square root of t).

source_evidence.locator: Optimization for Machine Learning / 5.3. Gradient Methods on Nonsmooth Problems / Proposition 5.6

children.title: Best-Iterate Guarantee
children.top_down_role: The guarantee family for the best objective value observed along a trajectory.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon guarantee for projected Euclidean subgradient descent with arbitrary positive stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex with minimizer \(x^*\), and generate \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_C(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\), where \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), \(\|g_k\|_2\le G\), and \(\alpha_k>0\). Then, for every \(T\ge1\), \[\min_{0\le k<T}\bigl(f(x_k)-f(x^*)\bigr)\le\frac{\|x_0-x^*\|_2^2+G^2\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\alpha_k^2}{2\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\alpha_k}.\] Writing \(R=\|x_0-x^*\|_2>0\), the constant choice \(\alpha_k=R/(G\sqrt T)\) gives \[\min_{0\le k<T}(f(x_k)-f(x^*))\le GR/\sqrt T.\] If \(R=0\), the initial point is already optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best objective value among the first T projected subgradient iterates satisfies an arbitrary-stepsize bound and an optimized order-one-over-square-root-T specialization.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\neq\varnothing\).
\(f\) is convex and every selected subgradient satisfies \(\|g_k\|_2\le G\).

notation.meaning: Uniform bound on selected subgradient norms.
Initial distance to the selected minimizer.

review_flags: Replaces the deferred unsourced seed and handles the zero-distance boundary of the optimized step explicitly.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Subgradient Best-Iterate Guarantee
Best-Iterate Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon guarantee for projected Euclidean subgradient descent with arbitrary positive stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex with minimizer \(x^*\). For \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), set \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_C(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\), where \(\alpha_k>0\) and \(\lVert g_k\rVert_2\leq G\). Then, for every integer \(T\geq1\), \[\min_{0\leq k<T}\bigl(f(x_k)-f(x^*)\bigr)\leq\frac{\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert_2^2+G^2\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\alpha_k^2}{2\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\alpha_k}.\] In particular, a constant choice \(\alpha_k=\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert_2/(G\sqrt{T})\) gives a bound of \(G\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert_2/\sqrt{T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best objective value among the first T projected subgradient iterates has a stepsize-dependent bound and reaches order one over square root of T with an optimized constant step.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\neq\varnothing\).
\(f\) is convex and \(\lVert g_k\rVert_2\leq G\) for every selected \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\).

notation.meaning: Uniform upper bound on selected subgradient norms.

children.title: Ergodic Subgradient Rate
children.top_down_role: The convergence family for uniform and weighted averaged outputs.

children.title: Euclidean Ergodic Regime
children.top_down_role: Averaged-output guarantees in Euclidean geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Ergodic Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-average guarantee for projected subgradient descent in Euclidean geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the projected subgradient iteration \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_C(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\), define \(A_T=\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\alpha_k\) and \(\bar x_T=A_T^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\alpha_kx_k\). If \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), \(\lVert g_k\rVert_2\leq G\), and \(x^*\) minimizes \(f\) over \(C\), then \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert_2^2+G^2\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\alpha_k^2}{2A_T}.\] Thus, when \(\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert_2\leq R\), taking \(\alpha_k=R/(G\sqrt{T})\) yields \(f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq RG/\sqrt{T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stepsize-weighted average obeys the same Euclidean energy bound as the best iterate and achieves an order-one-over-square-root-of-T objective gap.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex with a minimizer \(x^*\).

notation.meaning: Sum of the first T stepsizes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role and weighted Euclidean average match the terminal container. The claim is standard and internally consistent, but no source supports the precise iteration, weighting convention, or constants.

children.title: Mirror Ergodic Regime
children.top_down_role: Averaged-output guarantees in Bregman geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-average mirror-descent guarantee with explicit trajectory well-posedness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be convex in a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(h\) be differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\), and assume every update \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{\alpha_k\langle g_k,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_k)\}\] is attained in the differentiability domain of \(h\). If \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), \(\|g_k\|_*\le G\), \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_C f\), and \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{k<T}\alpha_kx_k)/(\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k)\), then \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{D_h(x^*,x_0)+\frac{G^2}{2\sigma}\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k^2}{\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stepsize-weighted mirror average is controlled by initial Bregman divergence and accumulated squared stepsizes.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on \(C\) and attains its minimum.
Every displayed mirror subproblem is attained in the differentiability domain, and \(\|g_k\|_*\le G\).
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Mirror Ergodic Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact Interior Sufficient Condition for Mirror-Step Well-Posedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete sufficient condition ensuring attained mirror steps and valid averages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(U\) is open, \(C\subset U\) is nonempty, compact, and convex, and \(h\in C^1(U)\) is strictly convex, then for every \(x_k\in C\), finite \(g_k\), and \(\alpha_k>0\), the mirror subproblem has a unique minimizer in \(C\subset U\). Every convex weighted average of the iterates also lies in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact convex domain inside the differentiability region of a strictly convex reference function guarantees unique attained mirror steps.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is open and \(C\subset U\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{\alpha_k\langle g_k,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_k)\}\text{ is a singleton in }C.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact Interior Sufficient Condition for Mirror-Step Well-Posedness
Mirror Ergodic Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-average mirror-descent guarantee under strong convexity of the reference function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be closed and convex in a finite-dimensional normed space, and let \(h\) be differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\). For \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), define \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{\alpha_k\langle g_k,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_k)\right\},\qquad \bar x_T=\frac{\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\alpha_kx_k}{\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\alpha_k}.\] If \(\lVert g_k\rVert_*\leq G\) and \(x^*\) minimizes \(f\), then \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{D_h(x^*,x_0)+\frac{G^2}{2\sigma}\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\alpha_k^2}{\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\alpha_k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mirror descent controls the objective gap of its stepsize-weighted average by initial Bregman divergence plus accumulated squared stepsizes.
assumptions_latex: \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and has a minimizer \(x^*\).
\(h\) is differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\).

notation.meaning: Dual norm corresponding to the primal norm.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role matches the Mirror Ergodic Regime. The stated estimate is plausible under standard mirror-descent regularity and well-posedness conditions, but no citation verifies those conditions or the factor 1/(2 sigma).

children.title: Diminishing-Stepsize Asymptotics
children.top_down_role: Asymptotic convergence families under vanishing schedules.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Summable Stepsizes Can Stall Before Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity boundary for infinite total travel in diminishing-step guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=|x|\) on \(\mathbb R\), \(x_0=1\), and let \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfy \(S:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k<1\). The subgradient trajectory using \(g_k=1\) is \(x_k=1-\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\alpha_j\to1-S>0\). Hence \(f(x_k)\not\to f^*=0\), even when \(\alpha_k\to0\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing, square-summable steps can stop short of the minimizer when their total length is finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Summable Stepsizes Can Stall Before Optimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ratio Criterion for Diminishing-Step Best-Value Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-value asymptotics under a cumulative ratio condition weaker than square summability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\), where \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), \(\|g_k\|\le G\), and \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_C f\) satisfies \(\|x_0-x^*\|\le R\). If \(\alpha_k>0\), \(A_T=\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k\to\infty\), and \(\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k^2/A_T\to0\), then \[0\le\min_{0\le k<T}f(x_k)-f^*\le\frac{R^2+G^2\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k^2}{2A_T}\longrightarrow0.\] In particular, \(\alpha_k\to0\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) imply the ratio condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best observed values converge when total step length diverges and accumulated squared steps are negligible relative to it; square summability is sufficient but unnecessary.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and convex \(f\) attains its minimum on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.title: Ratio Criterion for Diminishing-Step Best-Value Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Sequence Convergence Under Square-Summable Diminishing Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrected iterate-convergence variant with explicit lower-semicontinuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the setting of projected convex subgradient descent, assume additionally that \(f\) is lower semicontinuous on \(C\), \(\operatorname*{argmin}_C f\ne\varnothing\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\). If the selected subgradients are uniformly bounded, then \((x_k)\) is bounded, every cluster point is a minimizer, and in finite dimensions the full sequence converges to a point of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_C f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower semicontinuity, existence of a minimizer, bounded subgradients, and nonsummable square-summable steps make the full finite-dimensional trajectory converge to a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, convex, and lower semicontinuous and attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Sequence Convergence Under Square-Summable Diminishing Steps
Diminishing-Stepsize Asymptotics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic best-value convergence under nonsummable but square-summable stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex with nonempty solution set. Consider \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_C(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\), where \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) and \(\lVert g_k\rVert_2\leq G\). If \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\alpha_k\to0\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then \[\lim_{T\to\infty}\min_{0\leq k<T}f(x_k)=f^*,\qquad f^*=\min_{x\in C}f(x).\] Moreover, every cluster point of the iterate sequence is optimal; in finite dimensions the iterates converge to an element of the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsummable, square-summable stepsizes force the best observed value to the optimum; with bounded subgradients, cluster points are optimal and the finite-dimensional iterates converge.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on nonempty closed convex \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), with \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \min_{0\leq k<T}f(x_k)\to f^*\), and \(x_k\) converges to a minimizer.
review_flags: A source is needed to certify the stated iterate-convergence hypotheses.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits an asymptotic guarantee container. Best-value convergence is standard, but the stronger assertions about all cluster points and convergence of the full iterate sequence require a source confirming that the displayed hypotheses are sufficient.

children.title: Constant-Stepsize Neighborhood Guarantee
children.top_down_role: Persistent-scale convergence to an accuracy neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant Stepsize Need Not Converge Iteratively
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp iterate-level boundary for the running-best objective-neighborhood guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=|x|\) on \(\mathbb R\), constant-step subgradient descent with \(\alpha>0\), \(x_0=\alpha/2\), and \(g_k=\operatorname{sign}(x_k)\) has \(x_k=(-1)^k\alpha/2\). Consequently \(f(x_k)-f^*=\alpha/2\) for every \(k\), while the iterates form a nonconvergent two-cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed step on the absolute-value objective can produce a two-cycle whose objective error equals the asymptotic neighborhood scale.

notation.meaning: Sign of a nonzero real number.

knowledge_statements.title: Constant Stepsize Need Not Converge Iteratively
Constant-Stepsize Neighborhood Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon and asymptotic objective-neighborhood bounds for a fixed stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_C(x_k-\alpha g_k)\) with constant \(\alpha>0\), where \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), \(\lVert g_k\rVert_2\leq G\), and \(x^*\) minimizes convex \(f\) over closed convex \(C\). Then, for every \(T\geq1\), \[\min_{0\leq k<T}\bigl(f(x_k)-f(x^*)\bigr)\leq\frac{\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert_2^2}{2\alpha T}+\frac{\alpha G^2}{2}.\] Consequently, \[\limsup_{T\to\infty}\min_{0\leq k<T}\bigl(f(x_k)-f(x^*)\bigr)\leq\frac{\alpha G^2}{2},\] so a fixed stepsize guarantees approach to an objective neighborhood whose scale is proportional to \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant stepsize yields a transient term decreasing as one over T and a persistent objective error no larger than one half alpha times the squared subgradient bound.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and convex \(f\) has a minimizer \(x^*\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the container, and the finite-horizon best-value estimate is standard. No source is supplied, and the neighborhood interpretation must be understood as a guarantee for the running best objective value, not necessarily for every iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant-stepsize convergence to an objective neighborhood
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The notation \(f_\infty\) is inherited from the source's convergence analysis of the generated subgradient sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the subgradient-boundedness assumption hold, so that \(c\geq\sup_{k\geq0}\|g_k\|\), and let \(\alpha_k\equiv\alpha\). If \(f^*=-\infty\), then \(f_\infty=f^*\). If \(f^*>-\infty\), then \[f_\infty\leq f^*+\frac{\alpha c^2}{2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under bounded generated subgradients and a constant stepsize, an unbounded-below problem has asymptotic objective value minus infinity. When the optimal value is finite, the asymptotic objective lies within alpha times c squared over two of it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^*=-\infty\Rightarrow f_\infty=f^*;\qquad f^*>-\infty\Rightarrow f_\infty\leq f^*+\frac{\alpha c^2}{2}

children.title: Mirror Subgradient Convergence Guarantees

children.title: Bounded Dual-Norm Regime
children.top_down_role: The baseline mirror guarantee regime with controlled oracle magnitude.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Baseline constant-step rate under uniformly bounded dual-norm subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the preceding mirror update, suppose \(x^*\) minimizes convex \(f\), \(D_h(x^*,x_0)\le R_h^2\), and \(\|g_k\|_*\le G\). With a constant step \(\alpha>0\) and \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}x_k\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{R_h^2}{\alpha T}+\frac{\alpha G^2}{2\sigma}.\] For \(R_hG>0\), choosing \(\alpha=R_h\sqrt{2\sigma}/(G\sqrt T)\) yields \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{\sqrt2R_hG}{\sqrt{\sigma T}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded dual-norm subgradients give the mirror average an optimized order-one-over-square-root-of-T gap.
assumptions_latex: All mirror steps are attained in the differentiability domain of \(h\).
knowledge_statements.title: Optimized Bounded-Dual-Norm Mirror Rate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fundamental estimate for the baseline constrained mirror-subgradient update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\), and suppose \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in C}\{\alpha_k\langle g_k,z\rangle+D_h(z,x_k)\}\) is attained. Then, for every \(x\in C\), \[\alpha_k\langle g_k,x_k-x\rangle\le D_h(x,x_k)-D_h(x,x_{k+1})+\frac{\alpha_k^2}{2\sigma}\|g_k\|_*^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mirror step telescopes Bregman distance and incurs a quadratic error controlled by the selected vector's dual norm.
assumptions_latex: The displayed mirror subproblem is attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Dual-Norm Mirror One-Step Inequality
Bounded Dual-Norm Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Baseline mirror-subgradient rate with uniformly bounded dual-norm oracle outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), and suppose \(D_h(x^*,x_0)\leq R_h^2\). Apply mirror subgradient descent with a constant step \(\alpha>0\) for \(T\) iterations and return \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}x_k\). If \(\lVert g_k\rVert_*\leq G\), then \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{R_h^2}{\alpha T}+\frac{\alpha G^2}{2\sigma}.\] Choosing \(\alpha=R_h\sqrt{2\sigma}/(G\sqrt{T})\) gives \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{\sqrt{2}\,R_hG}{\sqrt{\sigma T}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded dual-norm subgradients give mirror descent an order-one-over-square-root-of-T averaged objective gap, scaled by the initial Bregman radius and reference curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on closed convex \(C\), has minimizer \(x^*\), and \(D_h(x^*,x_0)\leq R_h^2\).
\(h\) is differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{\sqrt{2}\,R_hG}{\sqrt{\sigma T}}\) for the optimized constant step.

notation.meaning: Upper bound on initial Bregman divergence to a minimizer.
Strong-convexity modulus of the reference function.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role matches the bounded dual-norm regime. The rate is plausible, but the statement does not explicitly display the mirror update and has no citation verifying the update convention, well-posedness assumptions, or optimized constant.

children.title: Relative-Geometry Regime
children.top_down_role: Mirror guarantees organized through reference-function-relative regularity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror-subgradient guarantee replacing uniform dual-norm boundedness by relative Lipschitz continuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume convex \(f\) is \(M\)-relatively Lipschitz according to the preceding convention, \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_C f\), and every update \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{\alpha_k\langle g_k,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_k)\}\] is attained where \(D_h\) is finite. Then, for \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) and \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{k<T}\alpha_kx_k)/(\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k)\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{D_h(x^*,x_0)+\frac{M^2}{2}\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k^2}{\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative Lipschitz continuity yields the standard weighted mirror gap bound without a global dual-norm bound.
assumptions_latex: The convention-fixed relative Lipschitz condition holds.
Every mirror step is attained and all required Bregman divergences are finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Geometry Mirror Ergodic Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Lipschitz Continuity in Bregman Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-fixed oracle-growth condition for this relative-geometry regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a differentiable convex reference function \(h\), a convex function \(f\) is \(M\)-relatively Lipschitz on \(C\) if, for every \(x,y\in C\) and every \(g\in\partial f(x)\), \[\langle g,x-y\rangle\le M\sqrt{2D_h(y,x)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative Lipschitz continuity bounds subgradient action by the square root of the reverse-point Bregman divergence.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and convex wherever the displayed divergence is used.

notation.meaning: Relative Lipschitz constant under this convention
Bregman divergence with base point x

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Lipschitz Continuity in Bregman Geometry
Relative-Geometry Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror-subgradient guarantee under relative Lipschitz continuity with respect to the reference divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be differentiable and convex on \(C\). Suppose convex \(f\) is \(M\)-relatively Lipschitz with respect to \(h\), meaning that for every \(x,y\in C\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\), \[\langle g,x-y\rangle\leq M\sqrt{2D_h(y,x)}.\] For the mirror update \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{\alpha_k\langle g_k,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_k)\}\), the weighted average \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{k<T}\alpha_kx_k)/(\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k)\) satisfies \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{D_h(x^*,x_0)+\frac{M^2}{2}\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k^2}{\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative Lipschitz continuity replaces a global dual-norm bound and yields the usual mirror averaged-gap estimate directly in the reference function’s geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex, \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex, and a minimizer \(x^*\) exists.
\(h\) is differentiable and its Bregman divergence is finite at the iterates and \(x^*\).
review_flags: A source is needed to certify this precise relative-Lipschitz convention and constant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the Relative-Geometry Regime. The precise relative-Lipschitz convention, the one-step mirror inequality needed for the displayed constant, and existence of the argmin update are source-sensitive and unsupported here.

children.title: Strongly Convex Mirror Regime
children.top_down_role: Curvature-enhanced mirror subgradient guarantees.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linearly Weighted Strongly Convex Mirror Rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature-enhanced mirror-subgradient rate with explicit indexing and averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\), let \(f\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\), and suppose \(\|g_k\|_*\le G\). For \(k=1,\ldots,T\), let \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{\alpha_k\langle g_k,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_k)\},\qquad \alpha_k=\frac{2}{\mu(k+1)},\] assume every update is attained, and define \(\bar x_T=\frac{2}{T(T+1)}\sum_{k=1}^T kx_k\). Then \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{2G^2}{\sigma\mu(T+1)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative objective curvature, decreasing steps, and linear averaging improve the bounded-oracle mirror rate to order one over T.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) attains its minimum and is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\).
\(h\) is differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex in the chosen norm.
\(\|g_k\|_*\le G\), and every displayed mirror step is attained.

notation.meaning: Linearly weighted average of x_1 through x_T

knowledge_statements.title: Linearly Weighted Strongly Convex Mirror Rate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Strong Convexity Relative to the Reference Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-fixed curvature assumption for the strongly convex mirror regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex function \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to differentiable convex \(h\) on \(C\) if, for every \(x,y\in C\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\), \[f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\mu D_h(y,x).\] This is objective curvature and is not implied merely by strong convexity of \(h\) in a norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative strong convexity adds a positive Bregman-curvature term to the objective subgradient inequality; curvature of the reference function alone does not provide it.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and convex on the relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Strong Convexity Relative to the Reference Function
Strongly Convex Mirror Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted mirror-subgradient rate under objective curvature relative to the reference function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\). Assume \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\): for every \(x,y\in C\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\), \[f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\mu D_h(y,x).\] Apply the mirror update with \(\alpha_k=2/(\mu(k+1))\), and form \(\bar x_T=2(T(T+1))^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{T}k x_k\). If \(\lVert g_k\rVert_*\leq G\), then the curvature-weighted analysis yields \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{2G^2}{\sigma\mu(T+1)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative strong convexity and linearly weighted averaging improve the mirror-subgradient objective rate from inverse square root to inverse T.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has a minimizer \(x^*\) and is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(h\).
\(h\) is differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\).

notation.meaning: Relative strong-convexity modulus of f with respect to h.
Linearly weighted average of mirror iterates.

review_flags: A source is needed to verify the precise indexing and constant in the relative-strong-convexity rate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role matches the curvature-enhanced mirror container. The O(1/T) claim is plausible, but the update itself is only referenced rather than defined, and the stepsize indexing, averaging weights, and constant require authoritative verification.

children.title: General Convex Gap Regime
children.top_down_role: Baseline averaged-output convergence for convex objectives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted averaged-output guarantee for fixed-scale regularized dual averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:C\to\mathbb R\) be nonnegative and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex, with \(\min_C h=0\). Given \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), weights \(a_t>0\), and \(s_t=\sum_{i=1}^t a_i g_i\), set \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta h(x)\}.\] If \(\|g_t\|_*\le G\), then, with \(A_T=\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\), \(S_T=\sum_{t=1}^T a_t^2\), and \(\bar x_T=A_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T a_tx_t\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{\beta h(x^*)+G^2S_T/(2\sigma\beta)}{A_T}.\] If \(h(x^*)>0\), the choice \(\beta=G\sqrt{S_T/(2\sigma h(x^*))}\) yields \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{G\sqrt{2h(x^*)S_T/\sigma}}{A_T}.\] For \(a_t=1\), this is \(G\sqrt{2h(x^*)/(\sigma T)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-scale dual averaging has a weighted comparator-regularization bound; balancing its two terms gives the canonical square-root rate.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty and convex, \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is convex, and \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_Cf\).
The displayed update minimizers exist, \(a_t>0\), \(\beta>0\), and \(\|g_t\|_*\le G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le[\beta h(x^*)+G^2S_T/(2\sigma\beta)]/A_T\), with the stated balanced specialization.
review_flags: A dedicated source should confirm this fixed-regularization dual-averaging convention and constants.
knowledge_statements.title: General Convex Dual-Averaging Gap Bound
General Convex Gap Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted averaged-gap bound for regularized dual averaging on a convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(\sigma\)-strongly convex, nonnegative, and minimized at \(x_1\) with value zero. Given \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), weights \(a_t>0\), and \(s_t=\sum_{i=1}^{t}a_i g_i\), regularized dual averaging sets \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{\langle s_t,x\rangle+\beta h(x)\right\}.\] If \(\lVert g_t\rVert_*\leq G\), then for \(A_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_t\) and \(\bar x_T=A_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_tx_t\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{\beta h(x^*)+\frac{G^2}{2\sigma\beta}\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_t^2}{A_T}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized dual averaging bounds the weighted averaged objective gap by comparator regularization plus accumulated squared weighted subgradient magnitudes.

notation.meaning: Regularization scale in the dual-averaging update.

review_flags: A dual-averaging theorem citation is missing, and the update convention requires source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the General Convex Gap Regime. The formula is plausible for a particular regularized dual-averaging convention, but no source verifies the fixed regularization scale, arbitrary weights, exact coefficient, or existence of the update minimizers.

children.title: Strong-Convexity Regime
children.top_down_role: Curvature-enhanced dual-averaging convergence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform- and increasing-weight guarantees for cumulative strongly convex lower models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex, let \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\) satisfy \(\|g_t\|_2\le G\), and define \(\ell_t(x)=\langle g_t,x\rangle+(\mu/2)\|x-x_t\|_2^2\). For weights \(a_t>0\), let \(A_t=\sum_{i=1}^t a_i\) and \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\sum_{i=1}^t a_i\ell_i(x).\] Then, for \(\bar x_T=A_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T a_tx_t\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{G^2}{2\mu A_T}\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{a_t^2}{A_t}.\] Uniform weights give \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{G^2(1+\log T)}{2\mu T},\] while \(a_t=t\) gives \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{2G^2}{\mu(T+1)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strongly convex lower-model dual averaging gives logarithmic-over-T convergence with uniform weights and order one-over-T convergence with increasing weights.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and the cumulative-model minimizers exist.
\(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\) and attains its minimum on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{G^2}{2\mu A_T}\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{a_t^2}{A_t}\), with the stated uniform- and increasing-weight specializations.

notation.meaning: Strongly convex lower model at round t.

review_flags: A dedicated source should confirm the cumulative-model convention and exact constants.
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Lower-Model Dual Averaging
Strong-Convexity Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logarithmic-regret dual averaging of strongly convex lower models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the Euclidean norm, with \(\lVert g_t\rVert_2\leq G\) for \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\). Define the quadratic lower model \(\ell_t(x)=\langle g_t,x\rangle+(\mu/2)\lVert x-x_t\rVert_2^2\), and generate dual-averaging iterates by \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\sum_{i=1}^{t}\ell_i(x).\] For the uniform average \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}x_t\), the strongly convex online-regret bound implies \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{G^2(1+\log T)}{2\mu T}.\] Thus curvature improves the general convex order \(T^{-1/2}\) rate to order \((\log T)/T\) for this unweighted output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual averaging of strongly convex lower models gives logarithmic cumulative regret and an averaged optimization gap of order log T over T.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(f\) has minimizer \(x^*\).

notation.meaning: Strongly convex quadratic lower model at the current iterate.
Uniform average of the first T iterates.

review_flags: A source is needed to certify the dual-averaging convention and exact logarithmic bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A complexity bound is the appropriate role for this terminal container. However, the proposed cumulative-lower-model update is convention-dependent, and no source establishes that it is the intended dual-averaging method or supports the exact logarithmic constant.

children.title: Online-to-Batch Regime
children.top_down_role: Conversion of cumulative online performance into an optimization guarantee.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected population-risk recovery from regret on independent sampled losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_T\) be independent and identically distributed, let \(\ell(\cdot;z)\) be convex on \(C\), and define \(F(x)=\mathbb E[\ell(x;Z)]\). Suppose \(x_t\) is measurable with respect to \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_{t-1}\), and \[\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\bigl(\ell(x_t;Z_t)-\ell(x^*;Z_t)\bigr)\right]\le R_T\] for deterministic \(a_t>0\) and \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_CF\). Then, for \(\bar x_T=A_T^{-1}\sum_ta_tx_t\), \[\mathbb E[F(\bar x_T)]-F(x^*)\le R_T/A_T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For predictable online decisions and i.i.d. losses, expected regret converts into expected population excess risk for the weighted average.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and each \(\ell(\cdot;z)\) is convex.
The samples are i.i.d., and \(x_t\) depends only on observations preceding round \(t\).
The relevant losses are integrable, the weights are deterministic and positive, and expected weighted regret is at most \(R_T\).
knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Online-to-Batch Conversion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of weighted optimization regret into a convex objective guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be convex, let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex, let \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_Cf\), and let \(x_t\in C\) with weights \(a_t>0\). If \[\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\bigl(f(x_t)-f(x^*)\bigr)\le R_T,\] then, for \(A_T=\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\) and \(\bar x_T=A_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T a_tx_t\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le R_T/A_T.\] The same inequality holds in expectation when the cumulative inequality holds in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity converts weighted cumulative optimization regret into an objective-gap bound for the corresponding average decision.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and \(f\) is convex with minimizer \(x^*\).
\(x_t\in C\), \(a_t>0\), and the weighted cumulative gap is at most \(R_T\).
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Weighted Online-to-Batch Conversion
Online-to-Batch Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of weighted online regret into a convex optimization guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, let \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\), and let an online method produce \(x_t\in C\) and positive weights \(a_t\). If its weighted optimization regret satisfies \[\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_t\bigl(f(x_t)-f(x^*)\bigr)\leq R_T,\] then the weighted batch output \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_tx_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_t)\) satisfies \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{R_T}{\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_t}.\] The same conclusion holds in expectation when the regret inequality holds in expectation and \(\bar x_T\) is random.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity converts weighted cumulative online regret into an objective-gap guarantee for the correspondingly weighted average iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex with minimizer \(x^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected-Risk Identity and Inequality for Online-to-Batch Outputs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected population risk of randomized and averaged online-to-batch outputs under IID sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_T$ be independent with common distribution $Q$, let $f_t(w)=c(w,\psi_t)$, and let $w_t$ be selected before observing $\psi_t$. Define $C(w)=\mathbb E_{\psi\sim Q}[c(w,\psi)]$. If $r$ is uniform on $\{1,\ldots,T\}$ and independent of the samples, then for $\bar w=w_r$,
\[
\mathbb E[C(\bar w)]=\mathbb E\!\left[\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(w_t)\right].
\]
If, additionally, $C$ is convex, then for $\bar w=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T w_t$,
\[
\mathbb E[C(\bar w)]\le \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(w_t)\right].
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly random selection of an online iterate has expected population risk exactly equal to the expected average incurred loss. If population risk is convex, the averaged iterate has expected population risk no larger than that quantity.
assumptions_latex: $\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_T$ are independent and identically distributed according to $Q$.
$f_t(w)=c(w,\psi_t)$ and $w_t$ is chosen before $\psi_t$ is observed.
For randomized output, $r$ is uniform on $\{1,\ldots,T\}$ and independent of the samples.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[C(w_r)]=\mathbb E\!\left[T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(w_t)\right],\qquad \mathbb E\!\left[C\!\left(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T w_t\right)\right]\le\mathbb E\!\left[T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(w_t)\right]\ \text{when $C$ is convex}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of online predictions into a stochastic output by averaging or uniform random selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given independent samples $\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_T\sim Q$, at round $t$ an online algorithm predicts $w_t$ and then receives the loss $f_t(w)=c(w,\psi_t)$. After $T$ rounds, output either
\[
\bar w=\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T w_t
\]
or $\bar w=w_r$, where $r$ is uniformly distributed on $\{1,\ldots,T\}$.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Online Regret to Expected Excess-Risk Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparator-wise conversion of average online regret into expected population excess risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the IID online-to-batch conditions, let the output be $\bar w=w_r$ with $r$ uniform on $\{1,\ldots,T\}$, or let $\bar w=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T w_t$ when $C$ is convex. Then, for every comparator $u$ in the common domain of $C$ and the losses,
\[
\mathbb E[C(\bar w)]-C(u)\le \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(f_t(w_t)-f_t(u)\bigr)\right].
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every comparator, the expected population excess risk of a valid online-to-batch output is at most the expected average online regret to that comparator.
assumptions_latex: $\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_T$ are IID from $Q$, $f_t(w)=c(w,\psi_t)$, and $w_t$ is selected before observing $\psi_t$.
The output is a uniformly randomized iterate, or it is the average iterate and $C$ is convex.
$u$ belongs to the common domain of $C$ and all $f_t$.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform terminal-window averaging for the strongly convex projected subgradient trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), let \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_C f\), and suppose \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) with \(\|g_k\|_2\le G\). Generate \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-2g_k/(\mu(k+1)))\). For fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\), let \(m_T=\lceil\rho T\rceil\) and \(\widehat x_T=(T-m_T+1)^{-1}\sum_{k=m_T}^T x_k\). Then \[f(\widehat x_T)-f(x^*)\le c_\rho\frac{G^2}{\mu T},\] where \(c_\rho<\infty\) depends only on \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging any fixed terminal fraction of the reciprocal-step trajectory gives an order-one-over-T objective gap.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(x^*\) exists.
