knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearly weighted output guarantee for strongly convex projected subgradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), and suppose \(\lVert g_k\rVert_2\leq G\) for every selected \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\). Starting from \(x_1\in C\), set \[x_{k+1}=\Pi_C\left(x_k-\frac{2}{\mu(k+1)}g_k\right),\qquad \bar x_T=\frac{2}{T(T+1)}\sum_{k=1}^{T}k x_k.\] If \(x^*\) minimizes \(f\) over \(C\), then \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{2G^2}{\mu(T+1)}.\] Hence linearly weighted averaging achieves an order-one-over-T objective gap without the logarithmic factor of uniform averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With reciprocal stepsizes and linearly increasing averaging weights, strongly convex projected subgradient descent attains an order-one-over-T objective gap.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(f\) has minimizer \(x^*\).
\(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the Euclidean norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Consequence of the Squared-Distance Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap consequence requiring a uniform subgradient bound on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every subgradient of \(f\) on \(C\) has norm at most \(G\), then \(f\) is \(G\)-Lipschitz on \(C\). Combined with \(\|x_{T+1}-x^*\|_2^2\le4G^2/(\mu^2(T+1))\), this gives \[0\le f(x_{T+1})-f(x^*)\le\frac{2G^2}{\mu\sqrt{T+1}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared-distance estimate implies an order-one-over-square-root-T objective bound under a uniform subgradient bound.
assumptions_latex: The deferred seed's squared-distance estimate holds.
Every subgradient of \(f\) on \(C\) has norm at most \(G\).
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Consequence of the Squared-Distance Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Squared-Distance Order Does Not Preserve Objective Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsmooth boundary on converting distance convergence into objective convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=|x|+\frac{\mu}{2}x^2\), the unique minimizer is \(0\), while \(f(x)-f(0)=|x|+O(x^2)\). Consequently, a sequence with \(|x_T|^2=O(T^{-1})\) can have only \(f(x_T)-f^*=O(T^{-1/2})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nonsmooth minimizer, objective excess may be linear in distance, so squared-distance and objective rates need not match.
knowledge_statements.title: Squared-Distance Order Does Not Preserve Objective Order

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selected-Iterate Subgradient Bounds Do Not Give Global Lipschitz Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on deriving objective last-iterate rates from distance rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bound \(\|g_t\|\le G\) only for subgradients selected along the algorithmic trajectory can suffice for a distance recursion, but it does not imply \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le G\|x-y\|\) for arbitrary \(x,y\in C\). Converting a last-iterate distance estimate into an objective estimate by Lipschitz continuity therefore requires a uniform subgradient bound on the relevant region, or another assumption directly controlling objective growth from the minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trajectory-only subgradient bounds may control distance but do not justify a global Lipschitz objective conversion.
assumptions_latex: Only the selected vectors \(g_t\) are assumed bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Iterate Subgradient Bounds Do Not Give Global Lipschitz Conversion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic nonergodic recursion for projected subgradient descent under strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a closed convex set \(C\), let \(x^*\) minimize \(f\) on \(C\), and set \(x_{t+1}=\Pi_C(x_t-\alpha_tg_t)\), where \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\) and \(\|g_t\|\le G\). Under the convention \(f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+(\mu/2)\|y-x\|^2\), \[\|x_{t+1}-x^*\|^2\le(1-2\mu\alpha_t)\|x_t-x^*\|^2+\alpha_t^2G^2.\] The recursion concerns the individual next iterate and uses no averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity and projection nonexpansiveness give a direct squared-distance recursion for each projected subgradient iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex under the displayed convention.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Step Last-Iterate Distance Recursion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonergodic distance guarantee for the curvature-scaled projected subgradient schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions of the corrected one-step recursion, choose \alpha_t=2/(\mu(t+1)) for t\ge1. Then every T\ge1 satisfies \[\|x_{T+1}-x^*\|^2\le\frac{4G^2}{\mu^2(T+1)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The curvature-scaled schedule gives order-one-over-T squared distance for the final projected subgradient iterate.
assumptions_latex: f is \mu-strongly convex on C under the \mu/2 convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Scaled Last-Iterate Distance Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonergodic objective order for the basic harmonic projected-subgradient schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C\subseteq\mathbb R^d be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let f:C\to\mathbb R be \mu-strongly convex under the \mu/2 convention. Suppose x^* minimizes f on C and the selected g_t\in\partial f(x_t) satisfy \|g_t\|_2\le G. For x_{t+1}=\Pi_C(x_t-g_t/(\mu t)), the last iterate satisfies \[f(x_T)-f(x^*)\le c\,\frac{G^2(1+\log T)}{\mu T}\qquad(T\ge2),\] for a universal numerical constant c independent of f,G,\mu,T, and d.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The basic harmonic schedule gives a logarithm-over-T objective guarantee for the final iterate.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}.
f\text{ is }\mu\text{-strongly convex under the }\mu/2\text{ convention}.
knowledge_statements.title: Harmonic-Schedule Last-Iterate Objective Bound
Strongly Convex Last-Iterate Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonergodic distance guarantee for projected subgradient descent with a curvature-dependent schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be closed and convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex with minimizer \(x^*\). Suppose \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\) and \(\lVert g_t\rVert_2\le G\). For the projected updates \(x_{t+1}=\Pi_C(x_t-\alpha_t g_t)\) with \(\alpha_t=2/(\mu(t+1))\), the individual iterates satisfy
\[\lVert x_{T+1}-x^*\rVert_2^2\le \frac{4G^2}{\mu^2(T+1)}.\]
Thus the last iterate, without averaging, converges to the unique minimizer in squared distance at rate \(O(T^{-1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With bounded subgradients and curvature-scaled steps, the final projected subgradient iterate has squared distance at most a constant times G²/(μ²T).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, finite, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on the closed convex set \(C\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the last-iterate container, but no citation supports the specialized stepsize, indexing, or constant 4. These details require an authoritative theorem-level locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected duplicate of the corrected individual-iterate recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the convention f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+(\mu/2)\|y-x\|^2, the proposed inequality was \|x_{t+1}-x^*\|^2\le(1-2\mu\alpha_t)\|x_t-x^*\|^2+\alpha_t^2G^2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The earlier coefficient one minus two times μ times the stepsize is incorrect under the stated μ-over-two strong-convexity convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The coefficient }1-2\mu\alpha_t\text{ is rejected; the valid coefficient is }1-\mu\alpha_t.

children.title: Stagewise Restart Policies

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total work of a geometric restart policy before specializing the growth law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta_s=q^s\Delta_0\), \(q\in(0,1)\), and \[m_s=\left\lceil B^2\frac{R(\Delta_s)^2}{\Delta_s^2}\right\rceil.\] If every stage certifies its next target and \(S=\min\{s:\Delta_s\le\varepsilon\}\), then \[S=\left\lceil\frac{\log(\Delta_0/\varepsilon)}{\log(1/q)}\right\rceil,\qquad N=\sum_{s=0}^{S-1}m_s\le S+B^2\sum_{s=0}^{S-1}\frac{R(\Delta_s)^2}{\Delta_s^2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total restart work is the sum of stage costs, with growth entering through the radius-to-gap ratio.
assumptions_latex: Every completed stage certifies the next prescribed gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Stage-Cost Aggregation Formula

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification needed before shrinking the localization radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A policy may invoke the next radius \(R(\Delta_{s+1})\) only after establishing \(f(x_{s+1})-f^*\le\Delta_{s+1}\). Without that certificate, the implication \(\operatorname{dist}(x_{s+1},X^*)\le R(\Delta_{s+1})\) is unavailable, so the localized inner-method contract cannot be applied inductively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking the restart radius without certifying the preceding gap breaks the restart induction.
assumptions_latex: The inner guarantee requires the current center to lie within its supplied radius of \(X^*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified-Restart Failure Boundary
Stagewise Restart Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic geometric restart scheme driven by a growth-to-radius bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume an inner method \(\mathcal A(x,R,m)\) returns \(y\) satisfying \(f(y)-f^*\le aGR/\sqrt m\) whenever \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le R\). Given \(x_0\), a certified gap \(f(x_0)-f^*\le\Delta_0\), a radius bound \(R(\Delta)\), and target \(\varepsilon\), set \(\Delta_s=2^{-s}\Delta_0\). At stage \(s\), choose
\[m_s=\left\lceil\left(\frac{2aG R(\Delta_s)}{\Delta_s}\right)^2\right\rceil,\qquad x_{s+1}=\mathcal A(x_s,R(\Delta_s),m_s).\]
Stop at the first \(S\) with \(\Delta_S\le\varepsilon\), and output \(x_S\). Then \(f(x_S)-f^*\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each stage halves a certified objective gap and selects its inner iteration count from the radius implied by the current growth bound.
assumptions_latex: The inner method satisfies the stated bounded-subgradient guarantee.
The initial gap bound \(\Delta_0\) and target \(\varepsilon>0\) are known.

notation.meaning: distance bound implied by gap Δ

children.title: Strong-Convexity Growth Regime
children.top_down_role: Restart behavior supported by strong-convexity growth.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric-restart complexity after substituting the strong-convexity radius law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(R(\Delta)=\sqrt{2\Delta/\mu}\), \(\Delta_{s+1}=q\Delta_s\) with \(q\in(0,1)\), and stage \(s\) uses at most \[m_s\le1+KG^2\frac{R(\Delta_s)^2}{\Delta_s^2}.\] For the first \(S\) with \(\Delta_S\le\varepsilon\), \[\sum_{s=0}^{S-1}m_s=O\!\left(\frac{G^2}{\mu\varepsilon}+\log\frac{\Delta_0}{\varepsilon}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth yields order G-squared over mu epsilon restart complexity.
assumptions_latex: The localized inner method obeys the displayed stage bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Convexity Restart Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Convexity Does Not Imply Bounded Subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample separating quadratic growth from the oracle bound used in subgradient complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f(x)=\frac{\mu}{2}\|x\|_2^2\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(\mathbb R^d\), but \(\|\nabla f(x)\|_2=\mu\|x\|_2\) is unbounded. Thus a finite \(G\) requires a bounded query region or a separate bound on queried subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity supplies growth but does not itself supply a global subgradient bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convexity Does Not Imply Bounded Subgradients
Strong-Convexity Growth Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic objective growth induced by strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a convex set \(C\), and suppose \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(X^*=\{x^*\}\) and
\[f(x)-f^*\ge \frac{\mu}{2}\lVert x-x^*\rVert_2^2\qquad\text{for every }x\in C.\]
Equivalently, every point with \(f(x)-f^*\le\Delta\) satisfies \(\lVert x-x^*\rVert_2\le\sqrt{2\Delta/\mu}\), which supplies the radius used by a stagewise restart policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity converts an objective-gap bound into a square-root distance bound, enabling progressively smaller restart regions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and \(f\) is proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(C\).

notation.meaning: minimum value of f on C
minimizer set, which is a singleton here

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic-growth statement is mathematically standard and the condition kind fits the container, but the record supplies no citation or locator supporting the stated strong-convexity convention and consequence.

children.title: Error-Bound Growth Regime
children.top_down_role: Restart behavior under objective-growth or error-bound structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle complexity obtained by inserting the Hölder radius law into a geometric restart schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\Delta_s=2^{-s}\Delta_0\), and stage \(s\) uses at most \(1+Kc^2G^2\Delta_s^{2\theta-2}\) oracle calls while certifying the next gap target. For the first \(S\) with \(\Delta_S\le\varepsilon\), \[N_S\le S+Kc^2G^2\sum_{s=0}^{S-1}\Delta_s^{2\theta-2}.\] Hence \(N_S=O(c^2G^2\varepsilon^{-2(1-\theta)}+\log(\Delta_0/\varepsilon))\) for \(0<\theta<1\), whereas \(N_S=O((c^2G^2+1)\log(\Delta_0/\varepsilon))\) for \(\theta=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric restarting has polynomial accuracy dependence below the sharp-growth endpoint and logarithmic dependence at the endpoint.
assumptions_latex: The radius law \(R(\Delta)=c\Delta^\theta\) is valid at every restart point.
The displayed per-stage inner-method bound holds.

notation.meaning: total oracle calls through stage S

knowledge_statements.title: Hölder-Growth Restart Complexity Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for using a local growth law along a restart trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the error bound is known only on \(L\), then \(f(x)-f^*\le\Delta\) justifies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le c\Delta^\theta\) only after establishing \(x\in L\). A gap certificate alone is insufficient unless its associated sublevel set is contained in \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local error bound supports restarting only while restart points are certified to remain in its validity region.
assumptions_latex: The Hölder error bound is asserted only on \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\notin L\Longrightarrow R(\Delta)=c\Delta^\theta\text{ is not certified by the local error bound}
knowledge_statements.title: Local Error-Bound Basin Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent power-growth formulation of the local Hölder objective error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c>0\), \(\theta\in(0,1]\), and every \(x\) in the stated validity region, \[\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le c(f(x)-f^*)^\theta\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(x)-f^*\ge c^{-1/\theta}\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^{1/\theta}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hölder distance error bound is exactly equivalent to a power-growth lower bound on objective excess.
assumptions_latex: \(c>0\), \(\theta\in(0,1]\), and \(f(x)\ge f^*\) on the validity region.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Objective-Growth Form
Error-Bound Growth Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hölderian error bound linking objective residual to distance from the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) have nonempty minimizer set \(X^*\) and minimum value \(f^*\). A Hölderian error bound with parameters \(c>0\) and \(\theta\in(0,1]\) holds on a sublevel region \(L\subseteq C\) when
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le c\bigl(f(x)-f^*\bigr)^\theta\qquad\text{for every }x\in L.\]
Consequently, a stage whose certified gap is at most \(\Delta\) may use radius \(R(\Delta)=c\Delta^\theta\); the resulting restart cost depends on the exponent through \(R(\Delta)^2/\Delta^2=c^2\Delta^{2\theta-2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hölder error bound turns each objective-gap target into a restart radius whose scaling is governed by the growth exponent.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and bounded below on \(C\).
\(X^*\ne\varnothing\) and the displayed inequality holds throughout the relevant sublevel region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(\Delta)=c\Delta^\theta\) is valid whenever the current iterate lies in \(L\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the error-bound growth leaf, but no source is cited for the chosen Hölder exponent convention or its use in the restart-cost formula.

children.title: Unknown-Growth Restarting
children.top_down_role: Restart policies operating without advance knowledge of growth parameters.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Comparison Is Not a Gap Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference between selecting the best observed objective and certifying its optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact comparisons of \(f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_M)\) identify \(\widehat x\in\arg\min_j f(x_j)\), but without \(f^*\) or a certified lower bound they do not provide a computable upper bound on \(f(\widehat x)-f^*\). Comparison can transfer a valid candidate's theoretical guarantee without certifying that guarantee from observed values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting the best candidate output is not an a posteriori optimality-gap certificate.
assumptions_latex: Only candidate objective values are observed.
No certified lower bound on \(f^*\) is available.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Comparison Is Not a Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of finite-grid adaptation to unknown growth parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Comparing outputs of candidate policies \(P_1,\ldots,P_M\) transfers a performance guarantee only if at least one candidate's assumptions hold for the actual objective. If every candidate is invalid, no bound \(B_j\) transfers regardless of how the output is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-grid adaptation works only relative to a candidate family containing a valid growth regime.
assumptions_latex: Each bound \(B_j\) is conditional on the assumptions of \(P_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall j,\ P_j\text{ invalid})\Longrightarrow\text{no candidate bound transfers}
knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Coverage Boundary
Unknown-Growth Restarting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dovetailed restart policies when the valid growth parameters are unknown.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal P=\{P_1,\ldots,P_M\}\) be a finite collection of restart policies corresponding to candidate growth parameters. Given a total budget \(T\), run each \(P_j\) independently for \(\lfloor T/M\rfloor\) oracle calls from the same initial point, producing \(x_j\), and output \(\widehat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le j\le M}f(x_j)\). If one candidate \(P_{j^*}\) is valid for the actual growth condition and has guarantee \(f(x_{j^*})-f^*\le B_{j^*}(\lfloor T/M\rfloor)\), then
\[f(\widehat x)-f^*\le B_{j^*}(\lfloor T/M\rfloor).\]
Thus unknown growth can be handled over a candidate grid at an oracle-budget factor of at most \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run restart schedules for several candidate growth laws in parallel and return the best objective value; the valid candidate controls the guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Objective values of candidate outputs can be compared exactly.
The finite candidate family contains at least one policy valid for the actual growth condition.
Each candidate receives the same initial point and oracle model.

notation.meaning: finite family of candidate restart policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-grid meta-algorithm is internally plausible and algorithm is the appropriate kind, but no source supports presenting this construction and its factor-M budget loss as the unknown-growth restarting regime.

children.title: Inexact-Oracle Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Convergence families accounting for deterministic error in value or subgradient information.

children.title: Persistent-Error Regime
children.top_down_role: Guarantees limited by nonvanishing deterministic error.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Additive Error Floor Is Sharp
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A stationary admissible execution attaining the additive epsilon-subgradient floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=|x|\) on \(\mathbb R\), fix \(\delta>0\), and take \(x_0=\delta\). The vector \(0\) belongs to \(\partial_\delta f(\delta)\). An oracle returning \(g_k=0\) at every iteration leaves \(x_k=\delta\), so \(f(x_k)-f^*=\delta\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A persistent-error oracle may return zero at a point whose objective gap equals its error budget, so the additive floor cannot generally be removed.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Additive Error Floor Is Sharp
Persistent-Error Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-iterate guarantee for subgradients with a nonvanishing additive oracle error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the oracle returns a \(\delta_t\)-subgradient \(g_t\), meaning \(f(y)\ge f(x_t)+\langle g_t,y-x_t\rangle-\delta_t\) for all \(y\in C\), with \(\lVert g_t\rVert_2\le G\). For \(x_{t+1}=\Pi_C(x_t-\alpha_tg_t)\) and \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_tx_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t)\),
\[f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le\frac{\lVert x_1-x^*\rVert_2^2+G^2\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t^2}{2\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t}+\frac{\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t\delta_t}{\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t}.\]
If \(\delta_t\equiv\delta>0\), this guarantee retains the additive floor \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A persistent additive subgradient error survives averaging as an additive accuracy floor, even when the ordinary optimization term vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is closed and convex, and \(f\) is convex on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_t\equiv\delta\) yields an upper bound equal to the exact-oracle term plus \(\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the persistent-error leaf, but the weighted inexact-subgradient inequality and additive floor lack an authoritative theorem or page locator.

children.title: Vanishing-Error Regime
children.top_down_role: Recovery of exact asymptotic behavior as oracle error decreases.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Error Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact asymptotic objective convergence under weighted decay of additive oracle errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the \(\delta_t\)-subgradient model and projected updates, let \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_tx_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t)\). If \(\lVert g_t\rVert_2\le G\), \(\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\alpha_t=\infty\), \(\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\alpha_t^2<\infty\), and
\[\frac{\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t\delta_t}{\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t}\longrightarrow0,\]
then
\[f(\bar x_T)\longrightarrow f^*.\]
In particular, the weighted-error condition holds whenever \(\delta_t\to0\), because the normalized positive weights form a Toeplitz averaging scheme whose denominator diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact objective convergence is recovered when the stepsize-weighted average oracle error vanishes and the usual diminishing-stepsize conditions hold.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a closed convex set and has a minimizer.
The stepsizes and errors satisfy the displayed summability and weighted-decay conditions.

notation.meaning: additive oracle error at iteration t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the vanishing-error regime and is internally coherent, but neither the inexact-oracle convergence result nor the Toeplitz-averaging implication has cited support.

children.title: Relative-Error Regime
children.top_down_role: Guarantees organized around error relative to oracle scale or progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Error Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle error controlled relative to the squared stepsize-oracle scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the additive \(\delta_t\)-subgradient model, suppose \(\delta_t\le\kappa\alpha_t\lVert g_t\rVert_2^2\) for some \(\kappa\ge0\), and \(\lVert g_t\rVert_2\le G\). Then the weighted average generated by projected subgradient updates satisfies
\[f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le\frac{\lVert x_1-x^*\rVert_2^2}{2\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t}+\left(\frac12+\kappa\right)G^2\frac{\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t^2}{\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t}.\]
Hence this relative error changes only the constant multiplying the exact-oracle accumulation term; it creates no independent persistent error floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If oracle error is proportional to stepsize times squared oracle magnitude, it is absorbed into the usual subgradient accumulation term.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a closed convex set and has a minimizer \(x^*\).
The projected method uses positive stepsizes and bounded \(\delta_t\)-subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x_T)-f^*\) obeys the displayed exact-rate bound with multiplier \(1/2+\kappa\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the relative-error leaf, but the particular definition δ_t≤κα_t‖g_t‖² and the resulting constant are model-specific and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Nonsmooth Convex Upper Bounds
children.top_down_role: Worst-case oracle guarantees achieved by Euclidean, mirror, and dual-averaging families.

children.title: Euclidean Lipschitz–Radius Complexity
children.top_down_role: Upper bounds expressed through Euclidean oracle and radius scales.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General projected-subgradient estimate for stepsize-weighted output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{t+1}=P_C(x_t-\alpha_tg_t)\), where \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), \(\|g_t\|_2\le G\), and \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_C f\). For \(\alpha_t>0\) and \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_tx_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t)\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le\frac{\|x_1-x^*\|_2^2+G^2\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t^2}{2\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t}.\] Thus averaged objective convergence follows if \(\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t\to\infty\) and \(\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t^2/\sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected subgradient descent with arbitrary positive steps has a radius-plus-squared-steps bound divided by cumulative step length.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f\) is convex on \(C\) and attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Stepsize Euclidean Upper Bound
Euclidean Lipschitz–Radius Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient upper bound on a Euclidean ball-scale domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex, let \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\), and suppose \(\lVert x_1-x^*\rVert_2\le R\) and \(\lVert g\rVert_2\le G\) for every queried \(g\in\partial f(x)\). With constant stepsize \(\alpha=R/(G\sqrt T)\), projected subgradient descent and the average \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^Tx_t\) satisfy
\[f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le\frac{RG}{\sqrt T}.\]
Therefore \(T\ge\lceil R^2G^2/\varepsilon^2\rceil\) first-order oracle calls suffice to produce an \(\varepsilon\)-suboptimal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected subgradient descent needs at most order (RG/ε)² oracle calls for a convex G-Lipschitz objective at Euclidean radius R.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f\) is convex and has a minimizer within distance \(R\) of \(x_1\).
All queried subgradients have Euclidean norm at most \(G\).

notation.meaning: initial Euclidean distance to a minimizer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind and Euclidean Lipschitz–radius formulation fit the container, but the exact averaged-iterate bound and oracle-call ceiling have no source locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-horizon best-iterate bound for normalized projected subgradient iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The estimate is a finite-horizon objective-gap bound under local Lipschitz continuity. The recurrence is meaningful while its selected subgradient is nonzero; the source does not specify a further update if an iterate at the minimizer has a zero subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:Q\to\mathbb R\) be Lipschitz continuous with constant \(M\) on \(B_2(x^*,R)\), and suppose \(x^*\in Q\) minimizes \(f\) on \(Q\), with \(f^*=f(x^*)\). Let \(x_0\in Q\) satisfy \(\|x_0-x^*\|\le R\), and let the iterates be generated by \[x_{i+1}=\pi_Q\!\left(x_i-h_i\frac{g(x_i)}{\|g(x_i)\|}\right),\qquad h_i>0,\quad g(x_i)\in\partial f(x_i),\] where \(g(x_i)\ne0\) whenever \(x_i\ne x^*\). Define \(f_k^*:=\min_{0\le i\le k}f(x_i)\). Then, for every \(k\ge0\), \[f_k^*-f^*\le M\frac{R^2+\sum_{i=0}^k h_i^2}{2\sum_{i=0}^k h_i}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For normalized projected subgradient iterates starting within distance R of a minimizer, local M-Lipschitz continuity bounds the best objective value seen through iteration k by M times the radius-and-step-size quotient.

children.title: Mirror Dual-Norm–Diameter Complexity
children.top_down_role: Upper bounds expressed through dual-norm oracle scale and Bregman domain size.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General dual-norm and Bregman-radius estimate for weighted mirror output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\). If mirror descent uses \(\eta_t>0\) and \(\|g_t\|_*\le G\), then for \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_tx_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t)\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{D_h(x^*,x_1)+\frac{G^2}{2\sigma}\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t^2}{\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t}.\] Averaged objective convergence follows if \(\sum_t\eta_t=\infty\) and \(\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t^2/\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t\to0\). Rescaling \(h\) and \(\sigma\) consistently preserves the intrinsic ratio \(D_h/\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The general mirror bound combines initial Bregman divergence with accumulated squared steps normalized by mirror-map strong convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a closed convex feasible set and attains its minimum.
\(h\) is differentiable at the relevant points and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex in \(\|\cdot\|\).
Mirror steps are well-defined, \(\eta_t>0\), and \(\|g_t\|_*\le G\).

notation.meaning: strong-convexity modulus of the mirror map

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Stepsize Mirror Upper Bound
Mirror Dual-Norm–Diameter Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror-descent upper bound using dual-norm subgradients and Bregman radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h\) be differentiable and 1-strongly convex with respect to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), and let \(D_h(x^*,x_1)\le\Omega\). Suppose every queried subgradient satisfies \(\lVert g_t\rVert_*\le G\). Mirror descent with constant stepsize \(\alpha=\sqrt{2\Omega}/(G\sqrt T)\) and average \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^Tx_t\) satisfies
\[f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le G\sqrt{\frac{2\Omega}{T}}.\]
Consequently, \(T\ge\lceil2G^2\Omega/\varepsilon^2\rceil\) mirror-oracle updates suffice for \(\varepsilon\)-suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mirror descent replaces Euclidean radius by Bregman radius and measures subgradients in the dual norm, retaining quadratic accuracy complexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a closed convex feasible set and has a minimizer \(x^*\).
\(h\) is differentiable and 1-strongly convex in the selected norm.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the mirror geometry leaf, but the mirror-descent update assumptions, normalization, and exact constant require a specific authoritative citation.

children.title: Strongly Convex Nonsmooth Complexity
children.top_down_role: Upper-bound families exploiting objective curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Averaging Can Retain a Logarithmic Factor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of what follows from pointwise inverse-time gap estimates under uniform averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\mathbb E[f(x_t)-f^*]\le C/t\). For \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^Tx_t\), convexity yields \[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_T)-f^*]\le\frac{C}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T\frac1t=\frac{CH_T}{T}\le\frac{C(1+\log T)}{T}.\] Thus pointwise \(O(1/t)\) bounds alone certify only a harmonic-factor bound for the uniform average; curvature-compatible weights, suffix averaging, or a sharper last-iterate argument are required to infer an \(O(1/T)\) guarantee by another route.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly averaging pointwise inverse-time guarantees introduces a harmonic logarithm.
assumptions_latex: The stated pointwise expected-gap bounds hold for \(t=1,\ldots,T\).
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Averaging Can Retain a Logarithmic Factor
Strongly Convex Nonsmooth Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature-dependent first-order upper bound for bounded-subgradient objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex and suppose every queried subgradient has norm at most \(G\). A curvature-weighted projected subgradient method using stepsizes proportional to \(1/(\mu t)\) and a correspondingly weighted average produces \(\widehat x_T\) satisfying
\[f(\widehat x_T)-f^*\le\frac{2G^2}{\mu(T+1)}.\]
Thus an \(\varepsilon\)-suboptimal point is obtainable with at most \(\lceil2G^2/(\mu\varepsilon)\rceil\) first-order oracle calls, up to the harmless indexing convention. The dependence improves from quadratic to linear in \(1/\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity improves bounded-subgradient oracle complexity from order ε⁻² to order G²/(με) when steps and averaging exploit curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is closed and convex, and \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(C\).
A minimizer exists and all queried subgradients have norm at most \(G\).
The method uses curvature-scaled diminishing steps and theorem-compatible weights.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asymptotic complexity order fits the leaf, but the method and averaging weights are not explicitly defined, and no citation supports the exact constant 2 or indexing convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly Convex Nonsmooth Rate via Uniform-Ball Smoothing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded convergence rate for Algorithm 6 under the Lipschitz and strong-convexity setting established by the surrounding smoothing construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(G\)-Lipschitz continuous and \(\alpha\)-strongly convex. For Algorithm 6, choose \(\delta=\frac{dG}{\alpha}\frac{\log t}{t}\). Then \(h_t=O\!\left(\frac{G^2d\log t}{\alpha t}\right)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a G-Lipschitz, alpha-strongly convex objective, Algorithm 6 with smoothing radius dG log(t)/(alpha t) attains source-defined error of order G squared d log(t)/(alpha t).

children.title: Large-Scale Lower-Bound Regime
children.top_down_role: Classical lower bounds before low-dimensional effects dominate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical deterministic lower bound when dimension grows at least linearly with the query budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist universal constants c,\kappa>0 such that for every T\ge1, G,R>0, and some Euclidean dimension d\ge\kappa T, every deterministic method using at most T calls to a local first-order oracle has an admissible convex G-Lipschitz objective on the radius-R Euclidean ball for which its output x_T satisfies \[f(x_T)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\ge c\frac{GR}{\sqrt T}.\] Equivalently, attaining worst-case error at most \varepsilon in this large-scale regime requires \Omega((GR/\varepsilon)^2) oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When dimension supplies linearly many hidden directions, deterministic local first-order methods cannot beat the GR over square-root-T nonsmooth rate.
assumptions_latex: The method is deterministic and uses a local first-order oracle.
The objective class is convex and G-Lipschitz on a Euclidean ball of radius R.
The ambient dimension is at least a universal constant times T.

notation.meaning: number of local first-order oracle calls

knowledge_statements.title: High-Dimensional Nonsmooth Oracle Lower Bound
Large-Scale Lower-Bound Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-dependent resisting-oracle lower bound before finite-dimensional localization becomes effective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, for every \(T\ge1\) and dimension \(d\ge2T\), any deterministic algorithm making at most \(T\) calls to a local first-order oracle has a convex function \(f\), defined on a Euclidean ball of radius \(R\), whose subgradients have norm at most \(G\), for which its output \(x_T\) satisfies
\[f(x_T)-\min_x f(x)\ge c\frac{GR}{\sqrt T}.\]
Hence worst-case oracle complexity is \(\Omega((GR/\varepsilon)^2)\) while the dimension is sufficiently large relative to the query budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In dimension proportional to the query budget, no deterministic local first-order method improves the worst-case GR/√T nonsmooth convex rate.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm is deterministic and accesses the objective through a local first-order oracle.
The adversarial class consists of convex \(G\)-Lipschitz functions on a Euclidean ball of radius \(R\).

notation.meaning: number of local first-order oracle calls

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the lower-bound regime, but the resisting-oracle model, universal constant, and threshold d≥2T are source-sensitive and have no cited theorem-level locator.

children.title: Finite-Dimensional Lower-Bound Regime
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds sensitive to ambient dimension and geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Lower-Bound Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension threshold for the classical deterministic resisting-oracle lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\ge 1\), \(R,L>0\), and \(d\ge T+1\). For every deterministic method that makes at most \(T\) calls to a local first-order oracle and returns \(x_T\) in the Euclidean ball \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|_2\le R\}\), there exist a convex \(L\)-Lipschitz function \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and a compatible oracle such that
\[
f(x_T)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\ge c\frac{LR}{\sqrt{T+1}},
\]
where \(c>0\) is a universal constant. The construction requires sufficiently many independent directions; hence this dimension-free-in-form lower bound does not by itself cover \(T\ge d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical nonsmooth lower bound scales as LR over square root T while dimension supplies at least one new resisting direction per query.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm is deterministic and accesses \(f\) through a local first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_T)-f^*\ge cLR/\sqrt{T+1}\) for a worst-case instance, with universal \(c>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the resisting-oracle model, the exact threshold d≥T+1, or the universal-constant lower bound. The failure_boundary kind is defensible because the statement emphasizes where the construction ceases to apply.

children.title: Strongly Convex Lower-Bound Regime
children.top_down_role: Information limitations after incorporating nonsmooth curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly Convex Nonsmooth Oracle Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic high-dimensional first-order lower bound for nonsmooth strongly convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist universal constants c,\kappa>0 such that for every T\ge1 and admissible G,\mu>0, some Euclidean dimension d\ge\kappa T, closed convex domain X, and \mu-strongly convex objective f on X with a local first-order oracle returning subgradients of norm at most G satisfy the following: every deterministic method using at most T oracle calls has an output x_T for which \[f(x_T)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\ge c\frac{G^2}{\mu(T+1)}.\] Thus worst-case error cannot decay faster than order 1/T in this nonsmooth strongly convex oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with strong convexity, deterministic nonsmooth first-order methods have a worst-case objective barrier proportional to G squared over μT.
assumptions_latex: The method is deterministic and uses a local first-order oracle.
The objective is \mu-strongly convex on a closed convex Euclidean domain.
The compatible oracle returns subgradients with norm at most G.
The ambient dimension is at least a universal constant times T.
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Nonsmooth Oracle Lower Bound
Strongly Convex Lower-Bound Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic first-order lower bound for Lipschitz strongly convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There is a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, for every \(T\ge1\) and every deterministic first-order method, a sufficiently large finite-dimensional Euclidean space contains a closed convex domain \(X\) and a convex function \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|_2^2,
\qquad \|g\|_2\le G,
\]
for all \(x,y\in X\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\), on which the method's output obeys
\[
f(x_T)-f^*\ge c\frac{G^2}{\mu(T+1)}.
\]
Thus strong convexity improves the nonsmooth error exponent from \(T^{-1/2}\) to \(T^{-1}\), but not beyond it in this oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with strong convexity, a nonsmooth first-order oracle cannot generally improve upon error proportional to G squared over μT.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a closed convex Euclidean domain.
The method is deterministic and makes at most \(T\) local first-order oracle calls.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An authoritative locator is required for the deterministic strongly convex nonsmooth lower bound, its bounded-subgradient formulation, and the required dimension. The complexity_bound kind fits the leaf.

children.title: Subgradient Oracle Optimality
children.top_down_role: Comparison of achieved upper bounds with black-box lower bounds.

children.title: General Nonsmooth Convex Optimality
children.top_down_role: Worst-case optimality of the classical nonsmooth first-order scale.

knowledge_statements.title: General Nonsmooth Convex Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax first-order complexity over bounded Lipschitz convex problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing a convex function \(f\) over a closed convex Euclidean set \(X\), with a minimizer \(x^*\) satisfying \(\|x_1-x^*\|_2\le R\) and oracle subgradients bounded by \(\|g_t\|_2\le G\). Projected subgradient descent with a tuned constant step and an averaged output satisfies
\[
f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le \frac{RG}{\sqrt T}.
\]
Conversely, when the ambient dimension is at least proportional to \(T\), every deterministic local first-order method has a worst-case error at least \(cRG/\sqrt T\). Consequently the minimax oracle complexity for error at most \(\varepsilon\) is
\[
\Theta\!\left(\frac{R^2G^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaged subgradient descent achieves the minimax nonsmooth convex scale: error Θ(RG/√T), equivalently Θ((RG/ε)²) oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and attains its minimum at \(x^*\in X\).
For the lower bound, the dimension is sufficiently large relative to \(T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The upper and lower bounds are standard in scale, but sources must establish a common problem class and oracle model before the stated minimax Θ conclusion is reliable.

children.title: Strongly Convex Nonsmooth Optimality
children.top_down_role: Worst-case optimality after incorporating objective curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distance Consequence of the Strongly Convex Objective Rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts the local objective-gap guarantee into a distance guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(X\), \(x^*\) minimizes \(f\) over \(X\), and \(f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le C G^2/(\mu(T+1))\), then \[f(\bar x_T)-f^*\ge\frac{\mu}{2}\|\bar x_T-x^*\|_2^2,\qquad \|\bar x_T-x^*\|_2^2\le\frac{2CG^2}{\mu^2(T+1)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse-linear objective rate implies an inverse-linear squared-distance rate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on the closed convex feasible set \(X\).
The stated objective-gap bound holds for \(\bar x_T\).
knowledge_statements.title: Distance Consequence of the Strongly Convex Objective Rate
Strongly Convex Nonsmooth Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax rate for bounded-subgradient strongly convex optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a closed convex Euclidean set, and suppose every queried subgradient has norm at most \(G\). A suitably weighted projected subgradient method with steps of order \(1/(\mu t)\) produces an output \(\bar x_T\) satisfying
\[
f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le C\frac{G^2}{\mu(T+1)}
\]
for a universal constant \(C\). In sufficiently large dimension, a deterministic first-order lower bound gives the same dependence up to a universal constant. Hence the minimax number of oracle calls needed to guarantee \(f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le\varepsilon\) is
\[
\Theta\!\left(\frac{G^2}{\mu\varepsilon}\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity changes the optimal nonsmooth rate to Θ(G²/(μT)), so ε accuracy requires Θ(G²/(με)) oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex and attains its minimum on \(X\).
The lower-bound statement uses a sufficiently large dimension and deterministic local oracles.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x_T)-f^*=\Theta(G^2/(\mu T))\) in the minimax sense, and \(T_\varepsilon=\Theta(G^2/(\mu\varepsilon))\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Matching sources are needed for the weighted projected-subgradient upper bound and deterministic lower bound, including the output convention and admissible problem class.

children.title: Geometry-Dependent Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity variation caused by norm choice, mirror map, and prox implementation.

children.title: Euclidean Dimension Dependence
children.top_down_role: Dimension effects induced by Euclidean radii and oracle norms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness of the dimension factor produced by separate maximum-norm bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(u=v=\mathbf 1\in\mathbb R^d\), \[\|u\|_\infty=\|v\|_\infty=1,\qquad \|u\|_2=\|v\|_2=\sqrt d.\] Thus both conversions from maximum norm to Euclidean norm can be tight simultaneously, and \(\|u\|_2\|v\|_2=d\). Without additional joint structure, the factor \(d\) cannot be improved from these two separate coordinatewise bounds alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All-ones vectors make both maximum-to-Euclidean norm conversions tight simultaneously.
assumptions_latex: Only separate maximum-norm bounds on the two vectors are used.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of Coordinatewise Euclidean Conversion
Euclidean Dimension Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension factors arising from Euclidean norm conversion in subgradient bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For Euclidean projected subgradient descent, the standard averaged-iterate guarantee is
\[
f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le \frac{R_2^2}{2\eta T}+\frac{\eta G_2^2}{2},
\qquad
R_2=\|x_1-x^*\|_2,
\quad G_2\ge\max_{t\le T}\|g_t\|_2.
\]
Choosing \(\eta=R_2/(G_2\sqrt T)\) gives \(R_2G_2/\sqrt T\). Dimension enters through norm conversion: if \(\|x_1-x^*\|_\infty\le R_\infty\) and \(\|g_t\|_\infty\le G_\infty\), then \(R_2\le\sqrt d\,R_\infty\) and \(G_2\le\sqrt d\,G_\infty\), yielding the possibly loose bound \(dR_\infty G_\infty/\sqrt T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Euclidean analysis is dimension-free in Euclidean parameters, but converting coordinatewise radius and subgradient bounds can introduce a factor d.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is closed and convex.
Projected subgradient iterates use a constant step \(\eta>0\).
The stated coordinatewise bounds hold when the norm-conversion conclusion is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le R_2G_2/\sqrt T\le dR_\infty G_\infty/\sqrt T\).

notation.meaning: distance bounds in Euclidean and maximum norms
subgradient bounds in Euclidean and maximum norms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The norm conversions and resulting factor d are mathematically consistent, but no inspectable source supports the projected-subgradient estimate or its geometry-dependent interpretation.

children.title: Mirror-Geometry Dimension Dependence
children.top_down_role: Improved or altered dimension dependence under domain-adapted geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Entropy Radius from the Uniform Center
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp logarithmic dimension factor for uniform-centered entropy geometry on the simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\Delta_d=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^d:\sum_i x_i=1\}\), let \(u=(1/d,\ldots,1/d)\) and \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^d x_i\log x_i\), with \(0\log0=0\). Then \[D_h(x,u)=\sum_{i=1}^d x_i\log(dx_i)=\log d-H(x),\] where \(H(x)=-\sum_i x_i\log x_i\). Consequently \(0\le D_h(x,u)\le\log d\), with equality at every simplex vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entropy divergence from the uniform simplex point has exact maximum log d at the vertices.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Entropy Radius from the Uniform Center
Mirror-Geometry Dimension Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mirror-descent bound and logarithmic simplex dependence under entropy geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be convex, let \(\psi\) be differentiable and \(1\)-strongly convex with respect to a norm \(\|\cdot\|\), and suppose \(\|g_t\|_*\le G_*\). If \(D_\psi(x^*,x_1)\le D\), mirror descent with a constant step \(\eta\) and averaged output satisfies
\[
f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le \frac{D}{\eta T}+\frac{\eta G_*^2}{2}.
\]
The choice \(\eta=\sqrt{2D}/(G_*\sqrt T)\) gives \(G_*\sqrt{2D/T}\). On the probability simplex, negative-entropy geometry initialized at the uniform point has \(D\le\log d\); hence the bound becomes \(G_*\sqrt{2\log(d)/T}\), replacing less favorable Euclidean dimension factors when gradients are naturally bounded in the dual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing entropy mirror geometry on the simplex can replace polynomial Euclidean dimension factors by a square-root logarithmic dependence.
assumptions_latex: \(\psi\) is differentiable and \(1\)-strongly convex relative to \(\|\cdot\|\).
For the simplex specialization, \(\psi\) is negative entropy and \(x_1\) is uniform.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le G_*\sqrt{2D/T}\), with \(D\le\log d\) for uniform-start entropy geometry on the simplex.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A source is required for the mirror-descent theorem and the negative-entropy simplex specialization, particularly the differentiability and boundary conventions.

children.title: Prox Cost–Iteration Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Tradeoff between favorable oracle complexity and per-iteration prox cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer guarantee exposing the effect of certified mirror-step errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose approximate mirror steps satisfy, for every \(x\in X\), \[\eta_t\langle g_t,x_t-x\rangle\le D_h(x,x_t)-D_h(x,x_{t+1})+\frac{\eta_t^2G_*^2}{2}+\delta_t,\qquad \delta_t\ge0,\] with \(\|g_t\|_*\le G_*\). For convex \(f\), \(g_t\in\partial f(x_t)\), and \(\bar x_T=(\sum_t\eta_tx_t)/(\sum_t\eta_t)\), \[f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\frac{D_h(x^*,x_1)+\frac{G_*^2}{2}\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t^2+\sum_{t=1}^T\delta_t}{\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified approximate-prox errors enter the mirror bound additively.
assumptions_latex: The displayed inexact mirror inequality holds for every comparison point.

notation.meaning: certified error in the one-step mirror inequality

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Prox Accuracy Accumulation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional end-to-end work bound coupling outer mirror accuracy to linearly convergent certified inner solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume D_h(x^*,x_1)\le D, \|g_t\|_*\le G_*, and the accepted inexact mirror inequality. For \varepsilon>0 choose \[T=\left\lceil\max\{1,8DG_*^2/\varepsilon^2\}\right\rceil,\qquad \eta=\frac{\sqrt{2D}}{G_*\sqrt T},\qquad \delta_t=\frac{\varepsilon\eta}{2}.\] Then f(\bar x_T)-f(x^*)\le\varepsilon. If an oracle call costs C_{\mathrm{orc}} and a certified \delta-accurate prox call costs at most A+B\log_+(1/\delta), where \log_+(u)=\max\{0,\log u\}, then \[W_T\le T\left[C_{\mathrm{orc}}+A+B\log_+\!\left(\frac{2}{\varepsilon\eta}\right)\right].\] For fixed D,G_*,C_{\mathrm{orc}},A,B, this is O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\varepsilon)) as \varepsilon\downarrow0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With logarithmic certified inner-solve cost, a uniform prox-error schedule gives epsilon accuracy in order epsilon-to-minus-two times log inverse epsilon total work.
assumptions_latex: Each approximate step satisfies the accepted one-step inexact mirror inequality.
A certified \delta-accurate prox call costs at most A+B\log_+(1/\delta).

notation.meaning: combined oracle and prox work through T iterations

knowledge_statements.title: Logarithmic-Cost Inexact-Prox Work Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General exact accounting that separates outer iteration count from oracle and prox costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a geometry \psi, let iteration t incur oracle cost C_{\mathrm{orc},t}, prox cost C_{\mathrm{prox},t}(\psi), and other implementation cost B_t. After T iterations, \[W_T(\psi)=\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(C_{\mathrm{orc},t}+C_{\mathrm{prox},t}(\psi)+B_t\bigr).\] Consequently, an iteration bound T_\varepsilon(\psi) determines an end-to-end work bound only after these per-iteration costs are bounded in a common computation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A geometry should be compared by combined oracle, prox, and maintenance work, not by iteration count alone.
assumptions_latex: All costs are measured in one specified computation model.
The stated components account for the implementation work under consideration.

notation.meaning: total work through T iterations using geometry \psi
iterations required for the declared accuracy guarantee

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Dependent Total-Work Accounting
Prox Cost–Iteration Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total-work accounting for geometry-dependent mirror or prox updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For mirror descent generated by \(\psi\), one iteration requires a subgradient evaluation and the prox computation
\[
x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\eta\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_\psi(x,x_t)\right\}.
\]
If their respective costs are \(C_{\mathrm{oracle}}\) and \(C_{\mathrm{prox}}(\psi,X)\), then \(T\) iterations cost
\[
W(T,\psi)=T\bigl(C_{\mathrm{oracle}}+C_{\mathrm{prox}}(\psi,X)\bigr).
\]
Under \(D_\psi(x^*,x_1)\le D_\psi^{\max}\) and \(\|g_t\|_*\le G_*\), sufficient iteration complexity is of order \(G_*^2D_\psi^{\max}/\varepsilon^2\). Thus geometry should be compared by total work \(W\), not iteration count alone: a smaller geometric factor can be offset by a more expensive prox subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A geometry reducing iteration count need not reduce runtime, because every mirror step also incurs its geometry-specific prox cost.
assumptions_latex: The prox minimization is solved exactly at cost \(C_{\mathrm{prox}}(\psi,X)\).

notation.meaning: cost of one exact prox computation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle and exact-prox work model fit the terminal container, but the iteration bound and additive per-iteration cost model have no cited support.

children.title: Parameter-Knowledge Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity distinctions caused by known or unknown scales, horizons, curvature, and target values.

children.title: Known-Scale Known-Horizon Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity for methods tuned with advance problem-scale information.

children.title: Known Problem-Scale Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity when relevant Lipschitz, radius, or geometric scale information is available.

knowledge_statements.title: Known Problem-Scale Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter information sufficient to normalize a constant subgradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume known positive bounds \(R\) and \(G\) satisfy \(\|x_1-x^*\|_2\le R\) and \(\|g_t\|_2\le G\). Knowledge of the problem-scale ratio \(R/G\) permits the normalized constant-step family
\[
\eta_T=\frac{R}{G\sqrt T}
\]
whenever a horizon \(T\) is subsequently specified. More generally, writing \(\eta=(R/G)a\) in the basic estimate
\[
f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le \frac{R^2}{2\eta T}+\frac{\eta G^2}{2}
\]
separates the scale information from the dimensionless tuning factor \(a\). Thus knowing \(R/G\) identifies the correct physical scale of the step, while horizon knowledge determines its \(T^{-1/2}\) decay.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Knowing the radius-to-subgradient ratio fixes the step-size scale; the horizon then supplies the dimensionless inverse-square-root factor.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and minimized at \(x^*\in X\).
Known bounds satisfy \(\|x_1-x^*\|_2\le R\) and \(\|g_t\|_2\le G\).
Projected subgradient descent uses an averaged output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R/G\) determines the dimensional scale of \(\eta\), while tuned horizon dependence gives \(\eta_T=R/(G\sqrt T)\).

notation.meaning: problem-scale ratio for the step size

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scale-separation calculation is coherent and the condition kind fits, but an inspectable source is required for the underlying averaged projected-subgradient estimate.

children.title: Known Horizon Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity when the planned iteration budget is available before execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Known Horizon Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Role of a declared terminal iteration in constant-step tuning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the terminal horizon \(T\ge1\) is known before the first update. For projected subgradient descent with constant step \(\eta>0\), initial-distance bound \(R\), and subgradient bound \(G\), the averaged iterate satisfies
\[
f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le \frac{R^2}{2\eta T}+\frac{\eta G^2}{2}.
\]
The horizon determines the balancing exponent: minimizing the right-hand side over \(\eta\) gives
\[
\eta_T=\frac{R}{G\sqrt T}.
\]
Thus advance knowledge of \(T\) permits one constant step to balance the initialization and accumulated-subgradient terms exactly at the declared stopping time; it does not by itself determine the multiplicative scale \(R/G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A known stopping horizon permits constant-step tuning proportional to T⁻¹ᐟ², provided the separate problem-scale ratio is available.
assumptions_latex: \(T\ge1\) is fixed before the iterations begin.
The output is the arithmetic average of projected subgradient iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_T=R/(G\sqrt T)\) minimizes the standard constant-step upper bound at horizon \(T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The horizon-balancing calculation is correct, but the standard constant-step guarantee lacks a source with a specific theorem, section, or page locator.

children.title: Jointly Tuned Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity for policies tuned using both problem scale and stopping horizon.

knowledge_statements.title: Jointly Tuned Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-step guarantee when scale and horizon are both known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be convex on a closed convex Euclidean set \(X\), let \(x^*\) minimize \(f\) over \(X\), and suppose \(\|x_1-x^*\|_2\le R\) and \(\|g_t\|_2\le G\). If \(R\), \(G\), and the horizon \(T\) are known, projected subgradient descent with
\[
\eta=\frac{R}{G\sqrt T},
\qquad
x_{t+1}=\Pi_X(x_t-\eta g_t),
\qquad
\bar x_T=\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T x_t
\]
satisfies
\[
f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le\frac{RG}{\sqrt T}.
\]
Consequently, choosing \(T\ge R^2G^2/\varepsilon^2\) guarantees \(\varepsilon\)-suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With radius, subgradient bound, and horizon jointly known, one constant step attains the standard RG/√T guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and attains a minimum \(x^*\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le RG/\sqrt T\), so \(T\ge R^2G^2/\varepsilon^2\) suffices for error at most \(\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The jointly tuned guarantee is internally consistent and the complexity_bound kind fits, but no source supports the projected-subgradient theorem and constants.

children.title: Scale-Misspecification Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Complexity effects caused by inaccurate advance scale information.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Misspecification Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact degradation factor from misspecified radius and subgradient scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume the true bounds are \(R\) and \(G\), but projected subgradient descent uses estimates \(\widehat R,\widehat G>0\) and the step
\[
\eta=\frac{\widehat R}{\widehat G\sqrt T}.
\]
Substitution into the constant-step estimate yields
\[
f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le\frac{RG}{2\sqrt T}\left(q+\frac1q\right),
\qquad
q=\frac{\widehat R G}{\widehat G R}.
\]
The multiplicative degradation relative to the correctly tuned bound \(RG/\sqrt T\) is therefore \((q+q^{-1})/2\ge1\). Only relative misspecification matters: multiplying both estimates by the same positive factor leaves the step and bound unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incorrect relative radius and gradient scales inflate the tuned bound by half the sum of their ratio and its reciprocal.
assumptions_latex: The true bounds satisfy \(\|x_1-x^*\|_2\le R\) and \(\|g_t\|_2\le G\).
The estimates \(\widehat R\) and \(\widehat G\) are positive.
A constant estimated-scale step and averaged output are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le (RG/(2\sqrt T))(q+q^{-1})\), where \(q=\widehat R G/(\widehat G R)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The substitution and degradation factor (q+q^{-1})/2 are algebraically consistent, but the underlying bound and sensitivity formulation lack cited support.

children.title: Unknown-Horizon Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity for anytime schedules and horizon-free certificates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Anytime Lower Bound by Fixed-Horizon Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise lower bound for algorithms required to produce an output at every stopping time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any anytime local first-order algorithm \(\mathcal A\) and fixed \(T\), stopping \(\mathcal A\) after \(T\) oracle calls produces an admissible fixed-horizon method. Hence the fixed-horizon lower bound transfers pointwise: on the bounded-subgradient convex class with scales \(R,G\), and in sufficiently large dimension, \[\sup_f\bigl(f(x_T^{\mathcal A})-f^*\bigr)\ge c\frac{RG}{\sqrt T}\] for a universal \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An anytime method stopped at a fixed time remains subject to the usual inverse-square-root oracle lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The anytime and fixed-horizon methods use the same local first-order oracle model.
The problem class has distance scale \(R\) and subgradient scale \(G\).
The dimension satisfies the fixed-horizon lower bound's requirement.

notation.meaning: algorithm producing an output after every number of oracle calls

knowledge_statements.title: Anytime Lower Bound by Fixed-Horizon Reduction
Unknown-Horizon Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Doubling schedule giving an anytime nonsmooth guarantee without a terminal horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume known \(R,G>0\), but no terminal horizon. Partition iterations into epochs of lengths \(m_k=2^k\), \(k=0,1,\ldots\). At the start of epoch \(k\), choose any fixed feasible restart point and use
\[
\eta_k=\frac{R}{G\sqrt{m_k}},
\qquad
x_{t+1}=\Pi_X(x_t-\eta_k g_t)
\]
throughout that epoch. At any time \(T\), output the arithmetic average of all iterates generated so far. If every restart point is within distance \(R\) of a common minimizer and \(\|g_t\|_2\le G\), summing the epochwise regret bounds gives
\[
f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le C\frac{RG}{\sqrt T}
\]
for a universal constant \(C\), without knowing \(T\) in advance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A doubling schedule removes advance horizon knowledge while preserving the optimal inverse-square-root rate up to a universal constant.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and has a minimizer \(x^*\in X\).
Every epoch restart satisfies \(\|x_{restart}-x^*\|_2\le R\), and \(\|g_t\|_2\le G\).
The bounds \(R,G\) are known, but the stopping horizon is not.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x_T)-f^*\le CRG/\sqrt T\) simultaneously for every stopping time \(T\ge1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but a source or complete authoritative statement is needed to validate the restart assumptions, all-iterate averaging, partial-epoch accounting, and simultaneous anytime guarantee.

children.title: Unknown-Curvature Unknown-Target Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity under unavailable curvature or objective-level information.

children.title: Unknown Curvature Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity when strong-convexity or related growth parameters are unavailable.

assumptions_latex: The oracle class consists of proper closed convex functions \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) on a closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\).
Every returned subgradient satisfies \(g\in\partial f(x)\) and \(\lVert g\rVert\leq G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The instance is in the unknown-curvature regime precisely when the method is not supplied with a valid value or positive lower bound for the largest \(\mu\geq0\) such that \(f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\) for all admissible \(x,y,g\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this oracle-information regime; an optimization-complexity source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-information condition allowing both merely convex and strongly convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An oracle instance has unknown curvature when \(f\) may be \(\mu\)-strongly convex for some \(\mu\geq0\), but neither \(\mu\) nor a certified positive lower bound for it is an input to the method. Thus each query reveals only local data such as \((f(x),g)\) with \(g\in\partial f(x)\); the policy must remain valid when \(\mu=0\) and cannot tune stepsizes, restart periods, or stopping rules using the true curvature modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method receives subgradient information but no certified curvature modulus, so it must work for both ordinary convex and strongly convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Unknown Curvature Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition matches the unknown-curvature container and is mathematically coherent, but no cited source establishes this oracle-information regime or its precise treatment of certified curvature lower bounds.

children.title: Unknown Target-Value Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity when the optimal objective level required by a tuned policy is unavailable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance-recursion effect of replacing the unavailable optimum value in a Polyak subgradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\in\arg\min_C f\), let \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\setminus\{0\}\), and choose a scalar target \(\tau\le f(x_k)\). For \(\alpha_k=(f(x_k)-\tau)/\|g_k\|^2\) and \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\),\n\[\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|^2\le \|x_k-x^*\|^2-\frac{(f(x_k)-f^*)^2-(\tau-f^*)^2}{\|g_k\|^2}.\]\nHence \(\tau=f^*\) gives the usual Polyak decrease, while an inexact target guarantees strict decrease from this bound only when \(f(x_k)-f^*>|\tau-f^*|\). If \(\tau>f(x_k)\), then \(\alpha_k<0\); the displayed recursion is no longer justified by the subgradient inequality, and the nominal update is not a forward subgradient step unless the policy is modified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative Polyak step using an inaccurate target incurs a squared target-error term and guarantees decrease only above that error; a target exceeding the current value makes the step negative and invalidates this recursion.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a nonempty closed convex set \(C\) and attains its minimum at \(x^*\).
\(\tau\le f(x_k)\), so \(\alpha_k\ge0\), for the stated distance recursion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|^2\le\|x_k-x^*\|^2-((f(x_k)-f^*)^2-(\tau-f^*)^2)/\|g_k\|^2\), with no such conclusion asserted for \(\tau>f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Polyak-Step Target Substitution Boundary

assumptions_latex: The optimal value \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\) is finite.
The method accesses only its stated first-order oracle and observed history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The instance is in the unknown-target regime when neither \(f^*\) nor any certified value equal to \(f^*\) is available to the policy.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly treats target-value knowledge in subgradient complexity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information regime for methods that cannot use the exact optimal objective level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)>-\infty\). The target value is unknown when the method is not supplied with \(f^*\), or with any certified scalar known to equal \(f^*\). Consequently, at iteration \(k\), a permissible stepsize and stopping decision must be measurable functions of the observed history \(\mathcal H_k\) and declared problem parameters, without evaluating an expression that requires the unavailable quantity \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimum is finite, but its objective value is unavailable; every update and stopping decision must use only observed history and declared parameters.
knowledge_statements.title: Unknown Target-Value Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly formalizes unavailability of the optimal objective value and fits the terminal container, but it has no inspectable citation supporting the stated information restriction.

children.title: Curvature-Adaptive Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies designed to accommodate unavailable curvature information.

assumptions_latex: For each curvature value \(\mu\) in a specified class, let \(B_T^{\mathrm{tuned}}(\mu)\) denote a valid guarantee for a policy given \(\mu\).
The adaptive policy receives no value or certified positive lower bound for \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A policy is curvature-adaptive when one parameter-free rule satisfies \(B_T^{\mathrm{ad}}(\mu)\leq c\,B_T^{\mathrm{tuned}}(\mu)\) for every admissible \(\mu\), up to explicitly stated logarithmic factors.

notation.meaning: Horizon-dependent guarantees of adaptive and tuned policies.

review_flags: The exact comparison criterion depends on the surrounding oracle model and requires a dedicated adaptive-complexity source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Performance-based definition relative to a curvature-tuned benchmark in the same oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an oracle model, output convention, and error criterion. A single policy is curvature-adaptive over a family indexed by \(\mu\) if it does not receive \(\mu\), remains valid for every admissible \(\mu\), and achieves a guarantee \(B_T^{\mathrm{ad}}(\mu)\) comparable to the curvature-tuned guarantee \(B_T^{\mathrm{tuned}}(\mu)\). Concretely, comparison requires \(B_T^{\mathrm{ad}}(\mu)\leq cB_T^{\mathrm{tuned}}(\mu)\) for a universal \(c\), with any permitted logarithmic overhead stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One policy is curvature-adaptive if, without knowing curvature, it nearly matches the guarantee of a policy tuned to every admissible curvature value.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Adaptive Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition has the correct role for a policy container, but the benchmark comparison, universal constant, and permitted logarithmic overhead depend on a specific oracle model and require a dedicated source before the mathematical definition can be fixed reliably.

children.title: Target-Free Stepsize Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies avoiding dependence on a known optimal objective value.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the available history is \(\mathcal H_k=\sigma(x_0,f(x_0),g_0,\ldots,x_k,f(x_k),g_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A stepsize policy is target-free exactly when \(\alpha_k\) is determined from \(\mathcal H_k\) and declared parameters without dependence on \(f^*\).
review_flags: A source specifically formalizing target-free subgradient policies is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-based definition, independent of any particular convergence rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For projected subgradient updates \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\), a stepsize policy is target-free if every \(\alpha_k\geq0\) is a deterministic or randomized function of the observed history \(\mathcal H_k\) and declared problem parameters, but not of the unavailable optimum value \(f^*\). Prescribed diminishing schedules, normalized rules, and history-adaptive rules qualify only when their formulas and parameter choices can be executed without inserting \(f^*\) or an uncertified surrogate asserted to equal it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A target-free stepsize can be computed from observations and known parameters without using the unknown optimal objective value or an asserted exact surrogate.
knowledge_statements.title: Target-Free Stepsize Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The information-based definition fits target-free stepsize policies and is internally consistent, but no source with a specific locator supports this formalization, including the treatment of randomized policies and uncertified surrogates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected from this leaf because the general diminishing-stepsize convergence theorem has its canonical home under subgradient convergence or diminishing-step policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(f\) be convex with nonempty solution set \(X^*\), and generate \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\), where \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) and \(\|g_k\|\le G\). If \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\alpha_k^2<\infty\), standard diminishing-step convergence conclusions hold under the usual projected-subgradient hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed theorem is a general diminishing-step convergence result rather than a statement primarily owned by target-value independence.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a nonempty closed convex set and attains its minimum.
The positive steps are nonsummable and square summable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The claim is deferred from this leaf on canonical-home grounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Target-Free Diminishing-Step Convergence

The proposed general diminishing-step convergence theorem is deferred as misplaced.
